items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 984Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. The fourth studio album of Porcupine Tree "Signify" that was released in 1996 is their first album with a fixed line up. Steven Wilson previously used various musicians to shape his compositions. "Signify" shows a clear transition phase from the band with the long instrumental tracks and lots of musical experiments to the more song orientated band. "Signify" presents a more mature approach than on "The Sky Moves Sideways", which doesn't mean better, having a stronger mix of styles. This is a relaxed work, generally slow and that doesn't have many hooks for the listener to grab on to. Its psychedelic sound is more ambient than ever, but I think isn't as deep as the wonderful "The Sky Moves Sideways".The line up on "Signify" is Steven Wilson (vocals, electric and acoustic guitars, samplers, tapes, organ, Mellotron, piano, drum programming, chimes and musical box), Richard Barbieri (piano, Hammond organ, tapes, sequencers and synthesizers Prophet-V and Roland System 700), Colin Edwin (bass and double bass guitars) and Chris Maitland (vocals, drums, cymbals, percussion, drum loops and keyboards. The work had the participation of Terumi (vocals) too.The original version of "Signify" has twelve tracks. "Signify" begins with "Bornlivedie" in which a narrator invites us to make ourselves comfortable to enjoy a soundscape that culminates with a female voice saying "Signify". "Signify" is the title track, where we actually can say that the album begins. It's an incredible paranoia inducing track, a hard riff, a pure electronic wonder and where a simple distorted solo from Wilson gives the atmosphere and rhythm. "The Sleep Of No Dreaming", as most of the songs of the album, has a very dark and brooding feel with lyrics chilling and sharp. It's a contrasting composition with the previous instrumental with quiet chords on the keyboards that set the dreamy mood for the track. "Pagan" is a quick transitory piece. It's a soundscape, an atmospheric piece, a guiding element between one theme and another. "Waiting Phase One" and "Waiting Phase Two" take up just over ten minutes. The first part starts with some acoustic chords and a few beats on the bass drum creating a peaceful moment, a kind of different peace. The second part is tribally enchanting due to the variety of sounds that emerge from it with a brief phrase on the piano and the tuneful touch on the guitar. The percussion and drums stand out within this psychedelic trance. "Sever" is where the harder progressive rock meets the electronic music. Maitland and Edwin are simply spectacular. It has a great chorus, with distorted voices crying out in despair, which makes this song another highlight on the album. "Idiot Prayer" has a pure electronic ambient. The band again approaches a different style and shows how eclectic they can be. Over a danceable rhythm, the guitar and keyboards move gracefully equally supported by an attractive percussion. "Every Home Is Wired" is a song that sounds more like a "Stupid Dream" or a "Lightbulb Sun" track. Here we have guitar and dreamlike keyboards under some echoing voices. Again the band is showing that this album can have it all. "Intermediate Jesus" is one of the biggest tracks on the album. It sounds like a kind of a jam that was included in the final material. This is an interesting instrumental, mostly improvisation, the only collective composition on the album. "Light Mass Prayers" is another ambient piece, but much longer than "Pagan". It has an atmospheric beginning, an ambient sound mainly through the keyboards. It's an exploration and experimentation by Wilson. "Dark Matter" is the lengthiest track on the album. It has some of the most brutal lyrics on the album, takes us out with an epic solo and some recollection and deep thought. This beautiful song, so dreamy and so awakening closes the album in a great way.The expanded remastered edition of "Signify" has 2 CD's. It comes with a bonus disc. The supplemental CD consists of demos recorded by the band between 1995-1996. This limited edition contains some extremely well developed, but still rough-on-the-edges demos and outtakes of "Signify". If you have any doubt about the quality of those tracks, rest assured. You don't get filler material here, but a fine complete album, which can hold a candle to the original release.Conclusion: Porcupine Tree occupies a very special place in the field of modern progressive rock and "Signify" is a great example of that. In reality, what we have here is a great addition to any progressive music collection. Basically all facets of the band on only one album are performed in high performance and with rich musicality. Overall, I loved the album and it's a great transition from their psychedelic space rock era, to a more modern progressive rock style which they later perfected. As I said before, "Signify" is the first Porcupine Tree's album where they sound like a band and not a Wilson's "vanity" project. It's a work where they forge their own unique sound and the foundation of their future albums "Stupid Dream" and "In Absentia". Nevertheless, regardless of it not being the best Porcupine Tree's album, this is a highly recommended work. Both challenging and accessible, this album surely has won over some new fans.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)
items._cn_summary: 这是Porcupine Tree乐队首张固定阵容专辑，标志乐队从纯器乐实验向歌曲化方向的过渡。专辑整体氛围松弛缓慢，迷幻声响比以往更偏环境化，但深度不及前作。Wilson在创作中承担多重角色，编曲融合电子合成器、采样、磁带效果与原声器乐。曲目设计强调氛围营造与段落之间的过渡，短小的器乐间奏串联不同主题，长篇幅作品在部落节奏与电子音效间构建仪式感。制作上呈现成熟的混音层次，将硬摇滚riff、电子实验与暗色调人声编织在一起。该专辑适合喜欢渐进式氛围铺陈的听众，但旋律钩子较少，需要耐心沉浸。

items.album: Death Drifts Under the Skin in Traitrs’ Video for “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong”
items.artist: “As We Dance With Tears in The Rain”

items.body: And I see your sadness Is it just like mine? We spend much of life rehearsing permanence. Calendars extend months ahead, plans multiply, and ordinary chores encourage the soothing fiction that tomorrow is already ours. Mortality remains manageable as long as it stays abstract, assigned to strangers or some distant version of ourselves. Grief breaks that arrangement. One absence can make every future date feel provisional, exposing distraction as one of the mind’s most useful shelters. “As We Dance With Tears in The Rain” — Death Drifts Under the Skin in Traitrs Video for “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong” That shelter is nearly universal. Work, desire, entertainment, ambition, and the small obligations of the day let us function while the knowledge of an ending waits at the edge of thought. When that knowledge presses forward, it carries a second fear with it: the possibility of losing every person, object, memory, and role through which we understand ourselves. Continuing to move after facing that fact can become its own form of courage. Toronto coldwave act TRAITRS confronts that contradiction in the new video for “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong,” released last November and later included on the band’s album POSSESSOR; the song begins with private anguish before reaching toward the possibility that another person’s grief may resemble our own. “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong is challenging The Psychology of Ignoring Death.” The recording begins beneath low, echoing synths, its measured dirge already gathering force. A disciplined drumbeat dances in the face of death, pulling the song forward as the guitars climb through serrated sweeps, widening melodies, and mounting sheets of effects. Shawn Tucker’s voice carries the cracked theatricality associated with Robert Smith and Brett Anderson while retaining its own bruised register, rising from a controlled ache toward the sound of a heart crying out against erasure. Each confession lands like a brick dropped onto a bare floor. The verses catalogue bodily harm through blunt images of starvation, wires, poison, and a fatal fall; the chorus turns outward, searching another person’s face for the same sorrow. There is a curious reversal within the arrangement: as the dirge-like synths grow heavier, the song seems to quicken, converting dread into momentum. Midway through, an organ-like phrase drives the track into a broader ascent before cascading vocals and guitars accumulate into a dense wall of sound, carrying the music to its greatest height precisely where the subject closes in on extinction. When the single first appeared, Tucker described the shared recognition at its center: “I felt that song connected me to everything and everyone, it is the one thing we all share and have in common,” Tucker said. “It is also a wake up call to live the life you want to live. We only have one chance at this so go dance in the rain.” Directed by Tucker and filmed in severe black and white, the video places Emmanuelle Vaughan inside a space without visible walls, floor, or horizon. She first appears at a distance beneath a narrow overhead light, nearly motionless, before the camera moves close to her collarbone, spine, hands, and face. An oil-dark coating begins to spread across her fingers, arms, back, and throat as her gestures become more expansive. Between these passages, Tucker performs at the microphone and guitar through smoke, coarse grain, and bands of video interference. Vaughan keeps dancing while her body is gradually claimed by the surrounding black, until the final movements yield to an empty frame. Tucker explains: “I find myself personally active in ignoring mortality. It’s inescapable and we use distraction as defence against it. We all crave purpose and everyday distractions. This is a psychological defense mechanism keeping our deepest fears at bay. Our fight for survival. Death has a way of playing with us, bringing up this deep sense of isolation and failure that we are all constantly running away from. Most people find the concept of being completely alone terrifying and painful. It’s stealing our tomorrows, it steals away everything. This album is incredibly personal for me because I’m still trying to make sense of a major loss in my own life. When I directed this, the goal was to visualize death as this unstoppable force—almost like a terminal illness creeping through the body. It doesn’t care who you are; it just destroys. But I didn’t want the video to just be bleak. It’s about our internal fight. I had wrapped the ‘Burn In Heaven’ video up a few months prior and was thinking about casting for I Was Ill and wanted to work with Emma again on this project as the lead and push her in a completely different approach. I also knew Emma knows exactly what I was looking for, and expected of her. In the video, she is aware death has come, but she still chooses to dance, finding this beautiful defiance right up until the black void completely takes over. It was all shot in one day on location in a small studio warehouse in Hamilton, Ontario, that took 7 hours.” The visual idea draws from Jonathan Glazer’s Under the Skin, particularly its limitless black chamber, where space loses every familiar coordinate and solitude becomes physical. Here, the setting turns mortality into an encroaching presence that can be seen on the body. Vaughan understands what has entered the room, yet her dance continues for as long as movement remains possible. “The void represented Ultimate Isolation perfectly and supports my visual theme of total isolation. There are no walls, no horizons, and no exit. The victims are entirely alone with their desires right before they are destroyed.” Tucker reduces the premise to one plain sentence: “None of us are getting out of here alive.” Within the song and video, that certainty becomes a reason to recognize another person’s sadness, inhabit the present, and dance while the body still answers. Watch the video for “I Was Ill, You Were Wrong” below: Formed in Toronto in 2015, TRAITRS began as a recording project before sessions with producer Josh Korody led to the 2016 debut Rites and Ritual. Butcher’s Coin followed in 2018, expanding the band’s audience across North America and Europe, while 2021’s Horses in the Abattoir brought another set of propulsive rhythms, angular guitars, and horror-informed electronics. Years of touring have carried TRAITRS through more than a dozen countries, including appearances at Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Castle Party, and Canadian Music Week, as well as shows with VNV Nation, Lebanon Hanover, She Past Away, Twin Tribes, and Ultra Sunn. POSSESSOR, released March 13, 2026, brings the band’s preoccupation with grief, alienation, and mortality into its most personal form to date. Recorded at Toronto’s Wychwood Studios with Josh Korody and mastered by Matt Colton, the album is available to stream here and order through Bandcamp here. items._cn_summary: 多伦多冷潮乐团TRAITRS在单曲《I Was Ill, You Were Wrong》中以低回回响的合成器、精确的鼓击与锯齿状吉他为骨架，将私人化的伤痛陈述编织为一场关于死亡、丧失与共情冥想。歌词以饥饿、电线、毒药、坠亡等直白意象铺陈肉体苦难，副歌则向外转向，试图在他者面孔中辨认相同的哀恸。编曲呈现有趣的倒置：合成器越沉重，音乐越加速，将恐惧转化为推进力，中段的管风琴式乐句将歌曲推向更开阔的攀升，叠层人声与吉他在主题逼近消亡处汇成密集音墙。主唱Shawn Tucker的声音兼具Robert Smith与Brett Anderson式的戏剧性裂痕，同时保有自身独有的淤伤质感。歌曲将死亡认知转化为生活行动的召唤，黑白影像的MV由Tucker执导，以严峻视觉呼应音乐的内省强度。

items.body: Thierry Kiranga was born in Katana, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, on the shores of Lake Kivu, and raised across the border in Bujumbura, Burundi, before civil war forced him to Italy. His new single, “Hard Times,” follows March’s “Ciao” and arrived July 17 on Roble Records. He learned to sing and to play guitar, drums and percussion under two Burundian mentors, Jean Christophe Matata and Canjo Amissi. Music ran in the family before that: his mother founded and still directs the Santa Cecilia choir, and his father sang tenor with the SOSAT choir and played violin on some of Italy’s earliest television broadcasts. Kiranga later studied Afro-Cuban jazz at Milan’s CPM conservatory, specialising in drums and percussion, and released his debut album, Asante, in the summer of 2023. “Hard Times” was recorded at Roble Factory Studio in Alghero, Sardinia, produced and mixed by Antonio Leardi and mastered by Simone Squillario. Choral harmonies sit over rhythms drawn from Kiranga’s Afro-Caribbean and European influences.The lyrics call out a broken promise: a world that claims to offer safety and prosperity while treating anyone different as a threat. Kiranga’s answer is to look to older generations for guidance, the same instinct that sent him to Matata and Amissi as a teenager and that he grew up watching in his own parents. On stage, Kiranga performs with an eight-piece band, The Backyard Embassy, drawing bass, guitar, keys, percussion, horns and backing vocals from players based across Italy, France, the US and Bulgaria. Stream “Hard Times” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Thierry – Hard Times appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: UK label Cold Spring releases the various-artists set “Noise” on 18 September 2026, collecting 22 tracks of harsh noise and electronics by musicians from mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan. The edition comes as a 2CD in an eight-panel glossy double digipak, with liner notes by Ban Yu. The set began life in 2012 as a China-only 2CDR carrying fifteen tracks, issued by Beijing’s Kwanyin Records. Cold Spring’s version adds seven further sets of works, some dating back as far as 2005, sequenced through the original running order rather than appended to it. Contributors include the Shanghai harsh-noise unit Torturing Nurse, Wang Changcun, Mei Zhiyong, Ronez, Taiwanese sound artist Fujui Wang, Orgasm Denial, Li Jianhong, Xu Cheng and Zafka. Cold Spring describes the material as “massive, piercing, and raucous – deliberately raw and disorienting”. The recordings come from a period when the work was solicited over the internet, through instant messaging, email and online noise groups, with most of the participants living in Beijing or Shanghai and building the tracks on software or hardware at home. Selection for this edition went by the actions and temperaments carried in the recordings rather than by chronology, which is why the added pieces sit inside the original running order. Noise (CSR376CD) by Various Artists Cold Spring ‘Noise’: the 22 tracks CD1: Shu Qi – “Get Rip Of Me” Yu Yiyi – “Free Nerve Ending” Ronez – “Cosmic Frog Bizarre Warfare” Dawang (Black Wolf) – “Untitled 2011121227” Mafeisan – “Meeting” Orgasm Denial – “Hawk Meets Penguin” Li ZengHui – “Thunder Child Crosses Electric Sea” GanzfeldLab – “14.99.17” Zafka – “Noise In Mind” Lao Dan – “This Is A Warning” Li Jianhong – “KG” Fujui Wang – “Pulsing Surds” CD2: Mei Zhiyong – “HaHaHa And The Red Sun” Xu Cheng – “STE-008” Wang Changcun – “Long Single Solid White Line” Zhou Risheng – “BIGNOISE” Beishanqnan – “Whispering Gossip Into A Cat’s Ear At A Party” Wa Hai Gui – “Que Tu Peux Me Faire Calmer” Li Yangyang – “Noise Shambhala” Zhang Yousheng – “The Dancing Girl” Torturing Nurse – “Turntable Contract” The Green Corpse – “POP (Light Version)” The 2CD is available to pre-order through the label’s webstore and Bandcamp. About Cold Spring Cold Spring was founded in 1990 by Justin Mitchell in England, after Mitchell had worked with Thee Temple ov Psychick Youth. The label started with cassette releases in the late 1980s, moved to vinyl and CD through the 1990s, and now issues physical and digital formats across power electronics, death industrial, dark ambient, neo-classical, neo-folk, soundtracks and experimental electronics. It operates from New Mills in Derbyshire. Its catalogue has drawn steadily on scenes outside western Europe, including Japanese noise and material from Russia, China and Poland. Recent Side-Line-covered items include the 1988 cassette compilation “Shoot And Crucify”, reissued on CD in July 2026 and remastered by Martin Bowes of Attrition; Hermann Kopp’s “Der Golem” soundtrack; the 10th-anniversary 2LP reissue of Coil’s “Backwards”; and the “Salò, or The 120 Days of Sodom” soundtrack, released in February 2026. “Noise” continues that reissue and archival strand, and brings a set that circulated only inside China in 2012 to general release.

items.body: “Our Love Will Live Forever” had its title before the event that made those words much harder to take literally. Jason Corbett took the phrase from his grandparents’ tombstone; only later, during the writing and recording of the album, a serious cardiac emergency forced him to consider whether he would finish the record at all, or return to the stage. His answer in this interview is strikingly unsentimental: “There is no permanence, there is no forever.” That does not negate the title so much as change the problem underneath it. “Our Love Will Live Forever”, ACTORS‘ third full-length album, due 4 September 2026 through Artoffact Records, becomes less about permanence as a promise than about what can remain meaningful once permanence itself is no longer credible. The new material emerged through “CTRL”, “Left On Read” and “Youth”, while Corbett’s enforced interruption gave the record a context he could not have planned when he began it. What is equally interesting, however, is how little Corbett wants to intellectualise his own process after the fact. Again and again, questions about control, rhythmic contradiction, genre or emotional design lead him back to instinct: the beat comes first, a song is left alone until it can be heard afresh, and technical decisions survive only if they produce an emotional reaction. Shannon Hemmett, meanwhile, gives the album’s central idea a visual counterpart through a star adapted from an engraving on medieval armour. The conversation moves between mortality and process, instant communication and old anxieties, authorship inside a four-person band, and what comes after the European tour. Youth by ACTORS Karo: “Our Love Will Live Forever” existed before the album acquired its most difficult context: the words come from your grandparents’ tombstone, and you had already chosen them before the cardiac emergency interrupted the record. I find that chronology fascinating because the sentence remained exactly the same while your relationship to it changed completely. When you returned to the album, did you feel that you were now making a different record underneath the same title? Jason: Yes and no. There were definitely challenges to this album that I had not experienced before. When you are forced to take a break like that, you can’t help but reevaluate your motivation and intentions. At the end of the day, there is no permanence, there is no forever. I’m lucky to be here making music. Karo: The cardiac emergency was serious enough that you were asking yourself whether you would finish the album or ever return to the stage. I’m less interested in the shock itself than in what happened when you went back to work. Did it change your threshold for what was worth keeping? Did anything suddenly feel too clever, too guarded or simply too unimportant to spend time on once not finishing the record had become a real possibility? Jason: It took some time for me to recalibrate and get my direction again. If anything, the whole situation gave me perspective. You can’t take yourself so seriously that it becomes stifling. The songs come from somewhere inside and outside of myself. I chose to continue trusting in my process. Karo: The album first became visible through “CTRL”, “Left On Read” and “Youth”, and to me they initially occupy quite different emotional spaces: compulsion and control, digitally prolonged rejection, then memory and the passage of time. Once they became parts of the same album, did you discover a connection between them that perhaps was not obvious while you were writing the individual songs? Jason: The songs naturally connect. Even the previous two albums were written over lengthy periods of time but were still cohesive. The commonality is that it’s all through my lens. That ties the music together. Karo: ACTORS are constantly described as “modern post-punk”, but I sometimes think “modern” has become one of those adjectives that explains almost nothing, particularly now that post-punk itself is such an established musical language. You’ve also said that you think less and less about genre. So what actually makes ACTORS contemporary to you now? Is it production, emotional language, technology, or simply the freedom not to treat the past as a set of instructions? Jason: Genre has become even more prevalent with the advent of streaming. We use modern post-punk as a recognisable jumping-off point for newcomers to our music. I think we operate artistically in the spirit of the first generation of post-punk, but we definitely have one foot firmly planted in the now. I don’t think about what other artists are doing. I’m interested in getting to the core of what we do. Karo: By now ACTORS have a sound that can be recognised very quickly, which is a huge achievement but potentially a dangerous one. Jason, you also produce the band yourself at Jacknife Sound, so you have an unusual degree of control over that identity. Have you ever made something technically good and unmistakably ACTORS and then deliberately damaged, changed or abandoned it because it felt too much like something you already knew how to do? Jason: All I think about is whether I like what I’m hearing. Is it eliciting an emotional reaction when I play it back? I will start work on a song, then leave it alone for a month, so when I come back to it, it tricks my mind into feeling like I’m collaborating with someone else. Then I get another level of creativity from the process. Karo: “Left On Read” takes something almost absurdly ordinary in contemporary communication and makes it psychologically cruel: silence is no longer simply absence, because you can see that your message has been received. I find that tiny technological change quite brutal. Has technology actually changed the experience of rejection and abandonment, or has it simply engineered a much more precise interface for anxieties people have always had? Jason: It’s the same feelings in a world that’s instant. The fact that we have access to each other 24/7 only expedites the emotional transaction. Karo: “CTRL” is intensely physical, with that very precise four-on-the-floor propulsion, while emotionally the song revolves around the absence of control. I like that contradiction because the body is being given something extremely disciplined to follow while everything underneath it is becoming less stable. How consciously do you use rhythm that way? Can musical control create a safe space in which emotional control can collapse? Jason: I couldn’t tell you. I’ve never analysed the elements of a song in that way. When I’m writing a song, the beat and vibe come first. Then I react to that and start writing the lyrics. It’s a natural process. Karo: One thing I keep noticing with ACTORS is how attractive the music can be while dealing with material that is not particularly comfortable. Melody, rhythm and production seduce first; sometimes the darker psychological content registers afterwards. But on this album there also seems to be a stronger movement back towards connection and life rather than simply dwelling inside damage. Has it become more difficult to write hope convincingly than darkness without making it sentimental? Jason: I hate to sound cliché, but the songs really do kind of arrive on their own schedule and with their own vibe. Once the spark hits, I do my best to craft it. You can say whatever you like. If that’s your honest expression, it should land. Karo: Shannon, you created the visual design for “Our Love Will Live Forever”. Here you were dealing with a title that already had an intensely personal history before you began giving the album a visual identity. What did you want the artwork to understand about the record without literally illustrating mortality, memory or love? And because the artwork comes from inside ACTORS, can you allow the visual language to disagree with the music rather than simply explain it? Shannon: The star design on the cover comes from an engraving on a medieval breastplate. To me, it was an ideal symbol to pair with the themes of the record. As the light from the star reaches into the dark, love becomes a form of armour and protection too. Karo: ACTORS have also allowed recent songs to be substantially reconstructed through remixes, from Dave Clarke‘s “In Real Life” to “Dead Inside (Crackmix)”. I always find the interesting remixes are the ones that stop behaving respectfully towards the original. When somebody else takes your song apart, how much do you actually want them to preserve? Is a misunderstanding sometimes more revealing than a faithful interpretation? Jason: I just love to hear what other artists do with a song. It’s fun to hear what their interpretations are. I’m not precious about it. Once the stems are out the door, they’re free to go wild. Karo: ACTORS originate with your songwriting and production, Jason, but live the project is unmistakably four people. Shannon, Kendall and Adam are not simply reproducing a finished studio object. After all these years of playing together, where does authorship begin to become collective? Can the live band teach you that something you considered fundamental to a recording actually wasn’t fundamental at all? Jason: Each member brings context and mood to the music. We exist on recordings and live onstage. Both are a different experience and important. The band members are an integral part of what the band and songs are. Karo: We’ll meet at NCN in Deutzen on September 5, almost at the beginning of the “Our Love Will Live Forever” tour. From there you have an extensive run through Germany, Rotterdam, Switzerland, Spain and Paris, followed by the UK shows with She Past Away and then Canadian dates in October. What happens after this announced run? Are you already discussing more European shows or festivals for 2027, and are there places where you particularly want to take this album that are not on the current schedule? Jason: After this fall tour, we have a bunch of US dates we will be announcing. That’s all I’m allowed to say. About ACTORS ACTORS are a Vancouver-based quartet consisting of Jason Corbett on vocals and guitar, Shannon Hemmett on synthesizers and vocals, Kendall Wooding on bass and vocals, and Adam Fink on drums. Corbett also produces the band’s music at his Vancouver studio, Jacknife Sound. The current line-up is confirmed by both the band and Artoffact Records. The band’s first full-length album, “It Will Come to You”, was released through Artoffact Records in 2018. Its combination of guitar, synthesizers, bass-driven momentum and tightly controlled production established the sound with which ACTORS became internationally associated. The follow-up, “Acts of Worship”, arrived on 1 October 2021, again produced by Corbett at Jacknife Sound. That album also marked Kendall Wooding’s first ACTORS album on bass. “Reanimated” followed in 2022, collecting earlier B-sides and related material, while the next period increasingly unfolded through individual releases. “In Real Life”, “Dead Inside” and “Object of Desire” appeared in 2024, followed by the “Crazy Lovers” remix collection in 2025. In 2026 ACTORS opened the new album cycle with “CTRL” in February, “Left On Read” in April and “Youth” in July. Their official Bandcamp currently lists those releases alongside the band’s earlier catalogue. Hemmett also records as Leathers, whose debut album “Ultraviolet” appeared in 2024. “Our Love Will Live Forever” is scheduled for 4 September 2026 through Artoffact Records. According to the album announcement supplied by the band, it is ACTORS’ third full-length studio album and was produced by Jason Corbett at Jacknife Sound. Shannon Hemmett created the album’s visual design. The album arrives simultaneously with a major touring period. The European run begins in Berlin on 4 September, followed the next day by NCN Festival in Deutzen. ACTORS then continue through Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Spain and France before three UK dates with She Past Away in Manchester, Bristol and London. Canadian shows follow in October in Vancouver, Edmonton and Calgary. And, as Corbett reveals here, that will not be the end of the 2026 live cycle: a further run of US dates is already planned, although the band is not yet ready to announce the details.
items._cn_summary: ACTORS 即将发行的第三张专辑《Our Love Will Live Forever》以主唱 Jason Corbett 祖父母墓志铭上的句子命名，却在录制期间因心脏急症而被迫中断，使得标题原本关于永恒的承诺转化为对无常的直面。专辑收录《CTRL》《Left On Read》《Youth》等曲目，创作过程强调直觉优先，节奏先行，技术决策以情感反应为唯一标准。贝斯手 Shannon Hemmett 为专辑设计的视觉核心来自中世纪盔甲上的星形纹饰，与歌曲主题形成跨越时空的呼应。文章通过采访形式探讨了四位成员乐队中的创作权归属、即时通讯时代的旧有焦虑，以及巡演之后的走向，整体呈现出一支暗潮乐队在生死命题下的冷静自省。Artoffact Records 作为发行厂牌保持了独立气质，与专辑内省基调契合。

items.body: You’ll be food for a hawk if you live like a lamb the hours decay like a corpse in the sand eternity calls and we’re singing for the damned There are records that announce their mortality with violins and candlelight, and then there are records that sound as if somebody has kicked open the crypt door. 1919’s Last Dance of the Departed, their first studio release since 2021 and first 7” since 1983, belongs to the latter breed: hard bass, serrated guitar, drums with the discipline of factory machinery, and Rio Goldhammer singing as though the end of civilization has inconvenienced him personally. 1919’s Bradford roots place them among the original wave of groups that pushed post-punk into darker territory during the early 1980s. Bands like Bauhaus and the Virgin Prunes were contemporaries in establishing what would later be called “goth”, working in parallel from different cities with a related vocabulary of skeletal guitars, theatrical dread, physical rhythm, and damaged religious imagery. On Last Dance of the Departed, 1919 carries that vocabulary forward with the blunt force of musicians who have spent years dragging these songs through clubs rather than preserving them behind glass. Ding Archer’s bass gives the track a heavy, stalking center, the guitar cuts across it in cold diagonal strokes, and the drums maintain a martial insistence that makes mortality feel strangely danceable. Last Dance of the Departed stares directly at extinction: brother killing brother, wages exchanged for useless possessions, gods who may have stopped answering the telephone, and the ridiculous persistence of hope. Goldhammer delivers these ideas with enough bite to prevent the song from collapsing into gothic sermonizing. There is black humour buried in the fatalism, the sort that develops when you have been around long enough to know death is coming so you may as well crank up the amp to give him a proper fanfare. The production leaves plenty of exposed bone. Guitar, bass, and percussion occupy their own hostile corners, colliding without becoming muddy, while Goldhammer rides above the racket with a voice closer to a public warning than a conventional rock performance. The video, directed by Goldhammer, pushes that idea into the flesh. Live footage flashes through a band still throwing itself at the stage after decades marked by departures and death. Members have been lost along the way, and the song carries that knowledge without converting grief into museum-piece reverence. These musicians still look dangerous because they remain committed to movement, volume, friction, and the communal absurdity of standing in a room together while the clock keeps chewing through time and space. Watch the video for Last Dance of the Departed below: For a band whose early history includes Cry Wolf, Machine, and two Peel sessions, 1919 sounds remarkably uninterested in reenacting 1983. Their post-punk remains angular and severe, but age has thickened the music’s sense of consequence. Last Dance of the Departed knows the party ends, knows the gods may be absent, knows the body goes back to ash, and still finds enough electricity in that knowledge to keep the dead dancing. 1919’s Last Dance of the Departed and its B-side Satellite Man are available on black and limited-edition green 7″ Vinyl. items._cn_summary: 1919 乐队自1983年以来首张7寸单曲《Last Dance of The Departed》，延续了英国后朋克与哥特摇滚的骨骼化美学。低沉的贝斯构成沉重追踪的核心，吉他以冷冽的对角线条切入，军鼓般的鼓点维持着近乎机械的节奏纪律。主唱 Rio Goldhammer 以近乎公共警告而非传统摇滚演唱的方式呈现歌词，主题直面末日意象：兄弟相残、薪俸换无用之物、神明可能已不再接听电话，以及希望的荒诞坚持。制作保留大量裸露棱角，三件乐器占据各自敌对角落而不致混浊。乐队早年与 Bauhaus、Virgin Prunes 同代，如今拒绝简单复刻1983年的声响，岁月使他们的后朋克变得更具棱角与厚重感，仍保持危险与运动中的承诺。

items.body: For the second episode of our Musical Road to WOMEX, we go from Caracas to Berlin by way of a conservatory in Barquisimeto, the route that shaped Gotopo into one of the more unclassifiable voices on the Afro-Latin Dance circuit. She runs Afro-Indigenous Venezuelan rhythm through techno production until neither side gives way, calls the result Ancestral Futurism, and stages it with a female-warrior aesthetic built as much for main-room dancefloors as festival fields. She started at the conservatory in Barquisimeto and came up through El Sistema, the youth-orchestra system that’s put instruments in the hands of generations of Venezuelan kids. She left for Berlin afterward and started over, busking to get by while she learned German. Her stage name comes from her own family history: Gotopo was the last indigenous chief of the region her family comes from. Nobody in her family had kept that history. She found it herself, digging through records nobody else had bothered to look at. She’s described the discovery as grief and celebration arriving together, something erased and something recovered in the same breath. Her 2023 debut EP, Sacúdete, followed, released on Waxploitation, the label built around Gnarls Barkley and Danger Mouse, with Don Elektron and Bomba Estéreo’s Simón Mejía among the collaborators. The reach has widened fast since. The title track ended up soundtracking Major League Soccer’s entire 2024 season, and a newer single, “Mi Gente Lo Siente,” is currently running under the trailer for Valorant Masters 2026. This October she brings that sound to Las Palmas de Gran Canaria at WOMEX’s Club Summit, the strand built around club and electronic sound from across the world. You trained in the conservatory and El Sistema, then found your own voice in Europe by reaching back to your Afro-Indigenous roots. What was the turning point that set that direction? When you take distance you start seeing things you never noticed before or comprehend them much deeper and from new points of view. The music conservatory planted in me a seed of discomfort of existing inside a music education that was so Eurocentric. Then ironically enough, it was Europe that gave me the space to explore how an ancestor of the future could exist in 202+. WOMEX lands this year in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, an Atlantic island whose timple itself carries old Latin American trade routes back across the ocean. As a Venezuelan artist, what are you most curious to discover about that shared history there? Because of the mass migration of Venezuelans I learnt that there’s a huge Canarian community in Venezuela spanning a few decades, people who saw in Venezuela a place to thrive, which it was, and now of course, it’s a reversed migration of kids and grand-kids back to Canaria… I’m obsessed with history and this one promises to be a huge adventure: What dishes will I taste here that will remind me of home? Or maybe slang words that were Venezuelan and landed here, or the opposite? It’s sooo weird in a cool way, I’m so curious! Your work fuses ritual and rave, the sacred and the synthetic. In a WOMEX programme full of traditions, what makes that fusion distinctly yours, and what do you want people to take from your showcase? Groove and vocals are the 2 cores of the most ancient musical memories we hold as humans… sometimes I think that we sang before we even spoke. I always want to make sure that my music makes you move, to me there is nothing more ancestral than groove, and in a Gotopo show you will hardly leave without having collectively sang along with a bunch of strangers WOMEX always sparks unexpected meetings. Which artists, labels or collaborators are you hoping to cross paths with in Las Palmas? There are festivals that I love because of their eclecticism and how they don’t care about Genre but rather about energy. THIS! This is so important for music, for culture and for human connection! I know the festival scene is going through challenging times for several reasons, specially the way kids discover and connect with music is changing… so I don’t blame festivals having to make tough decisions, and including upcoming acts in that equation is a challenge. But I also hope to see a future of festival/event curation where instead of falling for the extremes of either “play safe and book what the listener wants” or “I just book what I like”, promoters and bookers truly put an effort into understanding TikTok and new audiences and how these two are reprogramming people’s way to connect with culture. If you understand something you can hack it for your purpose, kinda, you know? It would be so sad if the curator’s experience of music and culture became isolated from the new generations. I do my job as an artist on social media, but curators, bookers and promoters who also understand this and actively work to stay up-to-date are definitely people I want to meet. Your live shows are as much performance and ritual as concert. How does a room of delegates change how you bring that energy? That’s a great question… I don’t think I want to change absolutely anything about my show. Gran Canaria sits at a mid-Atlantic crossroads between Africa, Europe and the Americas — exactly the between-worlds space you describe as a Latina in Germany. Does a place like that speak to your work? So much! And it makes me interested at a human level before anything, it’s an area I have yet to explore and it’s so exciting to perform in a place where there are so many ancient traces of you… of our constant migrations and cultural exchanges as humans which remind one another: this is what makes us pretty awesome as a humanity. If you could write a personal invitation to the people of Las Palmas to come and discover your showcase, what would it say? Have you heard about this girl from Venezuela? Some of her songs are catchy like Shakira but she’s a bit weirder.   Gotopo plays WOMEX 26's Club Summit in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria 21–25 October, at the Auditorio Alfredo Kraus   PLAYLIST: GOTOPO X RHYTHM PASSPORT   You can find all the previous episodes of Musical Road to Womex HERE   The post Musical Road to WOMEX 2026 – Gotopo appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由洛杉矶非营利音乐团体Los Cenzontles发起，联合夏威夷本土音乐人与Taj Mahal、David Hidalgo等资深乐手，将墨西哥与夏威夷的音乐传统进行深度对话。16首曲目涵盖老歌新译、新创作与美国民谣，尤克里里、吉他、墨西哥竖琴和手风琴的密集编排构成了统一的声音基底。录音在五天内以近乎现场的方式完成，保留了即兴与自发性，并穿插了Taj Mahal教授演奏的原始片段。对社会议题的触及体现在对伍迪·格思里《Deportee》的改编中，直面移民工人的现实处境。整体兼具文化历史厚度与即兴活力，是一次跨越语言和地域的真诚合作。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由芬兰手风琴家与钢琴家合作完成，35年的搭档默契让即兴对话显得自然流畅。大部分曲目仅为二人演奏，穿插无词人声，如开场传统曲目；标题曲加入弦乐四重奏，但编配克制。曲目包括传统作品、原创，以及皮亚佐拉的《Oblivion》和一首芬兰式探戈，整体在民谣、室内乐与探戈之间流动。乐评形容其具有梦境般的柔和气质，演奏以服务旋律为先，不求炫技，而重视探索与享受；对熟悉当代民谣或世界音乐的听众来说，是一种安静耐听的聆听体验。

items.album: Les Crimes du Musette
items.artist: Dominique Cravic et les Primitifs du futur
items.excerpt:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds

Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

Genuine Negro Jig

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组GuldGanger的出道EP，由经验丰富的民谣歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，收录五首以传统曲目为主的短作。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗粝的奔驰节奏展现主唱富有说服力的嗓音；《Nordgård》是唯一原创曲目，口簧琴与风笛带来持续推进感；《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》中钦巴龙营造精致背景，口簧琴则增添额外纹理；末曲《Ormsö》通过口簧琴与笛子、弦乐的混合，制造出既刺激又失衡的器乐效果。整张EP萦绕着古老而吱呀作响的独特氛围，器乐编排富有层次，是一支新乐队成熟而扎实的亮相。

items.body: Chilean band Amöniacö released the single “En algún momento” on 27 August 2026, the second track lifted from the re-recorded version of their 2011 debut album “Tu Fuego”. Carlos Vandal and Felipe Alarcón wrote the song, Vandal produced it at Noiser Studio in Santiago, and Fernando Cubillos mastered it at Riot Diva Studio. The song is not new. It sat fifth on the original “Tu Fuego”, released in October 2011, an album the band has said never got the promotion it needed at the time. Across 2025 and 2026 Amöniacö re-recorded, remixed and remastered the whole record, and a vinyl edition of the new version is planned. “En algún momento” follows “Aprendo a Morir (Sudden death version)”, issued on 8 May 2026 as the first preview, and pairs the same treatment with a restoration of the band’s earliest audiovisual material. Amöniacö mix alternative rock with post-punk and darkwave, and this track leans on the more atmospheric end of that: layered guitars, melodic lines and a driving rhythm underneath. The lyric deals with memories that return without permission, and with what stays behind after someone has gone. The single is on Spotify and across digital stores. It has not been posted to the band’s Bandcamp page, where the rest of the catalogue sits. What the Amöniacö ‘Tu Fuego’ relaunch covers The relaunch is a full re-recording rather than a remaster of the 2011 tapes. Every song from the original eleven-track album is being redone, with Vandal handling production at Noiser Studio and Cubillos mastering, the same pairing behind both singles released so far. Alongside the audio work, the band has restored the video material that goes with the earliest songs. The vinyl pressing has been confirmed but not dated. About Amöniacö Amöniacö began in the mid-2000s with Carlos Vandal writing the first songs, and put its first track, “Aprendo a Morir”, online in 2006. The band was formally constituted in Santiago de Chile in 2008. The current line-up is Vandal on vocals, guitars, bass and sequences, and Rod García on drums; the 2011 recordings featured Vandal with Jano Perverso on bass and Gabrielle on keyboards. The debut album “Tu Fuego” arrived in October 2011 with limited distribution. In 2012 the band reached the final of the Peugeot Music platform, and in April 2013 it opened for The Cure at the Estadio Nacional in Santiago on the group’s Latin American tour, selected by Robert Smith, who chose the support acts for each country himself. The single “Time to Change” followed, recorded and mixed by British engineer Barry Sage and mastered by Martin Bowes at The Cage Studios in Coventry. In 2015 Amöniacö played Lima with Cardenales and was selected for the third Converse Rubber Tracks call, which produced “No Volveré” with Pablo Giadach at Estudio Lautaro. “Castigarás” was recorded at Indómito Records with André Valenzuela, mastered by Mariano Pavez, played live in November 2017 and released digitally in January 2018. In 2017 the band joined the roster of the Santiago Noiser production company. The “Azul Prusia” EP, produced by José Ignacio Jaras, followed and was later taken into the catalogue of Cleopatra Records in the United States. Through the early 2020s the band issued the singles “Ritos”, “And Then It Rains” and “Regrets”, and in April 2024 opened for Clan of Xymox at Blondie in Santiago. “Live at Unisono”, recorded at Gustavo Cerati’s Estudio Unísono in Buenos Aires and mixed and mastered by Fernando Cubillos, came out in February 2025, and later that year the band issued a version of Soda Stereo’s “Canción Animal” through Scent Air Records. The “Tu Fuego” re-recording began in 2025, and “En algún momento” is its second instalment.
items._cn_summary: 智利乐队 Amöniacö 重新录制了2011年的首张专辑《Tu Fuego》，新单曲《En algún momento》保留了原曲但采用了全新的制作处理，由 Carlos Vandal 在圣地亚哥的 Noiser Studio 重新制作，Fernando Cubillos 在 Riot Diva Studio 完成母带处理。这是一次完整的重录而非简单重制，乐队同时修复了与早期歌曲配套的影像资料，并计划发行黑胶版本。音乐风格融合另类摇滚、后朋克与暗潮，这首作品偏向氛围感较强的方向，使用层次分明的吉他与旋律线条，搭配持续推进的节奏。歌词围绕不受控回涌的记忆与失去后残存之物展开。作为曾为 The Cure 拉丁美洲巡演暖场的智利独立乐队，Amöniacö 带有拉丁美洲地下音乐场景的独特视角，重录项目也为这张当年缺乏推广的处女作赋予了新的表达语境。

items.body: German electronic composer Michael Brückner released “The Egg in the Cosmic Crack” through the Argentine label Cyclical Dreams on 28 August 2026. The album runs six tracks and 77 minutes of Berlin School sequencing and ambient, and is out on digital platforms, as a download and on CD. Two of those tracks are almost twenty years old. The opener “The Egg of Ecquirlo” began as a giveaway Brückner made in 2007 for members of a Last.fm group he had founded, a track he kept meaning to place on a proper album. “Cracked Egg Mystification” came out of the same set of preoccupations and went to the Cerebral Audio compilation “The Rift: Volume 1” in 2016. Both were remixed, partly rearranged, remastered and given new detail for this release. From unused material left over from the 2007 sessions, plus fresh parts, Brückner assembled “The Egg of Ecquirlo – Part 2”, then recorded further pieces to complete the record. The thread running through all of it is a book. Brückner started making music at 21, prompted by meditative yoga practice, and through those studies read Joseph Chilton Pearce’s “The Crack in the Cosmic Egg”. Cyclical Dreams describes the result as “music based on the idea of the egg as a universal symbol”, and the album notes report that those early influences still inform Brückner’s music decades on. There is wordplay underneath the concept. The word “eye” appears in two of the titles, “Joseph’s Eye” and “The Eye of Cyclops”, and sounds like the German “Ei”, meaning egg. Brückner built the album on a wide spread of hardware and software instruments: the Waldorf Blofeld, Behringer DeepMind 6 and Model D, Moog Labyrinth, Korg Z1, NI Absynth, Cherry Audio Rhodes Chroma, GX-80 and Elka-X, u-he Hive 2 and the Moog Theremini. Cyclical Dreams handled the artwork, with photography by Amp Puttipong. The Egg in the Cosmic Crack by Michael Brückner Michael Brückner’s six tracks and where to hear them “The Egg of Ecquirlo – Part 1” (22:23) “Coda (A Pure Oval Shape)” (4:54) “Joseph’s Eye” (13:28) “Cracked Egg Mystification (Revisited)” (13:52) “The Egg of Ecquirlo – Part 2” (10:08) “The Eye of Cyclops” (12:49) The album is on Bandcamp and across digital platforms, with a download edition through Payhip and a CD pressed on demand through the label’s Kunaki storefront. Cyclical Dreams has also put the full album on YouTube. About Michael Brückner Michael Brückner was born in Heidelberg in 1969 and settled near Mainz, where he works as a graphic designer. He began composing and recording electronic music in 1992 without formal training, after the experience of mantra chanting in a yoga group, and started circulating his work through online networks from 2006. His output has run to well over a hundred albums, most of them downloads and CDrs, and he has performed live at smaller festivals and solo since 2012. His music sits mainly in ambient and Berlin School, with long sequenced passages and drifting synth layers. He records with several groups alongside his solo work, including P’Faun, Bridge To Imla and La Mansarde Hérmetique, and has collaborated with Mathias Grassow, Volker Lankow and Mathias Brüssel among others. Brückner has released steadily through Cyclical Dreams, the Buenos Aires label whose catalogue covers Berlin School, ambient, soundscape, space music and drone. His albums for it include “Footprints”, “Recycled Life”, “Twenty-Five Light Years”, “The Morphic Cycle”, “The Seven Planes of Dreams” in 2024 and “A Sequence of Colours” in December 2025. Side-Line has followed the label’s recent output, including D*Time’s “Nightwoven” and Christian Wittman‘s “Andromeda”. “The Egg in the Cosmic Crack” reaches further back than any of them, finishing a piece of music Brückner has carried since 2007.
items._cn_summary: 德国电子音乐人Michael Brückner发行专辑《The Egg in the Cosmic Crack》，由阿根廷小厂牌Cyclical Dreams发行。专辑包含六首曲目，总时长77分钟，以柏林学派序列化和氛围音乐为主。创作灵感源自Joseph Chilton Pearce的著作《The Crack in the Cosmic Egg》，以"蛋"作为宇宙象征贯穿全作，其中曲目标题中的"eye"与德语"Ei"（意为蛋）构成双关。专辑使用了Waldorf Blofeld、Moog Labyrinth、Korg Z1、u-he Hive 2等多种硬件与软件合成器，融合冥想瑜伽带来的早期影响。两首曲目源自近二十年前的旧作，经过重新混音、编曲与母带处理后收入，其余为新录音材料。作为信息性新闻发布而非深度乐评，文章侧重介绍创作背景、器材与发行信息。

items.body: Buzz Kull released a video for “In the Cut” on 26 August 2026, two weeks before the Sydney project starts a North American tour with Kontravoid. The track comes from “Deep Hate”, the EP Marc Dwyer issued through Heartworm Press on 13 February 2026. Chris Fatseas directed the video, which puts Dwyer opposite Sydney model Andrea. Buzz Kull’s ‘Deep Hate’ EP and its remix edition “Deep Hate” holds four tracks: “Black Gate”, “In The Cut”, “Just A Memory” and “Human Force”. Dwyer wrote and recorded all four, Ewan Kay mixed and mastered them, and Jonathan Schenke added mixing on “In The Cut”. Wes Eisold of Cold Cave sings on “Human Force”, which also carries an additional drum mix by Alex Garcia-Rivera. Amy Lee handled design and Shaun Daniel the photography. Heartworm Press pressed the EP as a 12-inch at 45 RPM in a black-and-white split variant and in a red-and-black marble “Bloodlust” edition limited to 100 copies. The CD and digital editions add four remixes: “Black Gate” reworked by PIG, “In The Cut” by Kontravoid, “Just A Memory” by Cold Cave and “Human Force” by Spike Hellis. Buzz Kull and Kontravoid tour dates The co-headline run opens on 10 September at Elysium in Austin as part of Levitation and closes on 24 October at Below at The Belasco in Los Angeles. Normal Bias supports the Brooklyn show, and Spike Hellis and Normal Bias join the Spokane, Vancouver, Seattle, Portland and Sacramento dates. 10 September 2026 – Austin, TX, US – Elysium (Levitation) 11 September 2026 – Houston, TX, US – Barbarella 12 September 2026 – New Orleans, LA, US – Santos Bar 13 September 2026 – Atlanta, GA, US – The EARL 15 September 2026 – Tampa, FL, US – The Orpheum 16 September 2026 – Orlando, FL, US – Will’s Pub 18 September 2026 – Baltimore, MD, US – Metro Baltimore 19 September 2026 – Philadelphia, PA, US – Nikki Lopez 20 September 2026 – Brooklyn, NY, US – Saint Vitus 22 September 2026 – Montreal, QC, Canada – Foufounes Electriques 24 September 2026 – Toronto, ON, Canada – Cafeteria 25 September 2026 – Millvale, PA, US – The Funhouse at Mr. Smalls 26 September 2026 – Milwaukee, WI, US – Anodyne Coffee Roasting Co. 28 September 2026 – Minneapolis, MN, US – Icehouse 1 October 2026 – Indianapolis, IN, US – The 808 at Indy CD & Vinyl 2 October 2026 – Kansas City, MO, US – Encore at Uptown 3 October 2026 – Denver, CO, US – HQ 4 October 2026 – Salt Lake City, UT, US – Metro Music Hall 6 October 2026 – Spokane, WA, US – The Big Dipper 8 October 2026 – Vancouver, BC, Canada – Biltmore Cabaret 9 October 2026 – Seattle, WA, US – El Corazon 10 October 2026 – Portland, OR, US – Star Theater 13 October 2026 – Reno, NV, US – The Holland Project 15 October 2026 – Sacramento, CA, US – The Starlet Room 16 October 2026 – Las Vegas, NV, US – Backstage Bar & Billiards 23 October 2026 – San Francisco, CA, US – Great American Music Hall (Substance) 24 October 2026 – Los Angeles, CA, US – Below at The Belasco (Substance) Side-Line published the tour announcement in Buzz Kull and Kontravoid announce 2026 North American tour. About Buzz Kull Buzz Kull is the solo project of Sydney musician Marc Dwyer, active since 2012. He mixes darkwave, EBM and minimal synth, and has worked with Rebecca Liston in the live line-up. The project’s first singles, “I Disappear” and “Dreams”, appeared through Fabrika Records in 2013 and 2014. The debut album “Chroma” followed in 2017 and “New Kind of Cross” in 2018, with a run of singles including “Nausea”, “Avoiding The Light”, “Last In The Club”, “Rise From Yur Grave” and “Dancing With Machines” issued through Avant! Records between 2017 and 2022. Side-Line covered the return in Australia’s dark electro act Buzz Kull returns with all new album, the first new work since 2019, which announced the third album “Fascination” on Avant! Records in 2022. Dwyer moved to Eskimo Recordings for the 2023 single “A Place That’s Meant To Be”, then to Cleopatra Records for four singles across 2024 and 2025. “Just A Memory” opened his run on Heartworm Press in 2025 and led into “Deep Hate”, his first release for the label, in February 2026. The “In the Cut” video is the project’s latest, arriving as the North American dates begin.

After more than 20 years, this is only the third album from the German EBM project. Several years have elapsed between releases, making each album feel somewhat like a new beginning, although I don’t think the EBM audience ever truly forgot T.A.N.K. “Broken Mirror” is the first album in nine years and also the project’s first release on Electro Aggression Recor
items.body: Reinhard Hüber brought T.A.N.K. to life in 2001 as a solo project, later joined by additional members for live performances. After more than 20 years, this is only the third album from the German EBM project. Several years have elapsed between releases, making each album feel somewhat like a new beginning, although I don’t think the EBM audience ever truly forgot T.A.N.K. “Broken Mirror” is the first album in nine years and also the project’s first release on Electro Aggression Records. It features 13 tracks plus five remixes and even a cover version. T.A.N.K. stands for vintage EBM—tracks that drive straight ahead. Typical heavy EBM basslines are paired with dark string arrangements, all set to a danceable rhythm. Here and there, a brief respite appears in the form of a slower tempo, where the EBM takes on a more atmospheric quality. Perhaps slightly atypical is Hüber’s harder, deep, distorted vocal style. While this is more common in Dark Electro productions, it works perfectly here. Among the tracks, I have a particular soft spot for “Zombie March” and its hilarious lyrics. After all, EBM rarely features profound lyrics—and that’s not something I personally expect from the genre anyway! Remixes were provided by Pyrroline, Sleepwalk, Serpents, Synaptic Defect, and Trilogy. The intelligent remix by Pyrroline, in particular, is an absolute treat for the ears. Finally, we get a somewhat surprising cover of R010R’s “Bloodsucker,” recast in a dark EBM mould. T.A.N.K. strikes back again with a solid, old-school EBM record that has been well crafted. Perhaps it could have been a bit harder overall for my taste, but otherwise, I have no complaints. (Rating:7½). Side-Line reported the announcement in April 2026, when Electro Aggression Records set “Broken Mirror” for release on May 30. Listen to “Zombie March”: Zombie March by T.A.N.K. About T.A.N.K. Reinhard Hüber, who came out of the 1990s German punk scene, launched T.A.N.K. in Dessau in 2001. The name stands for “Taktischer Angriff (auf’s) Nervenkostüm”. The first live appearance took place at the first Electric Tremor Festival in Dessau on 22 March 2002. The self-released “T.A.N.K.” EP landed in 2002, followed by the debut album “Musica Denaturale” on Ars Electrique in 2003. In 2011 the project contributed “Game of Men” to the 4CD set “Old School Electrology Volume One”. The second full-length, “Return”, came out in 2017 on Electric Tremor Dessau. Hüber also turned up in the Electro Aggression Records orbit through remix work connected to R010R and Synaptic Defect. “Broken Mirror” is the project’s third album and holds 19 tracks.
items._cn_summary: 这张《Broken Mirror》是德国EBM老牌项目T.A.N.K.的第三张正式专辑，历时九年才得以面世，发行于独立厂牌Electro Aggression Records。专辑收录13首原创曲目加5首remix和1首翻唱，共计19轨。音乐风格以vintage EBM为核心：重型贝斯线直击前方，暗色弦乐编排铺底，节奏强调舞池可听性。间或出现慢速段落，带有氛围化的EBM质感。主唱Hüber的嗓音偏向深沉的失真处理，更接近Dark Electro的路数，与音乐框架契合度良好。曲目《Zombie March》的歌词带有幽默感，刻意保持非深刻姿态。Pyrroline的remix版本在制作上明显胜出，呈现出更具层次感的听感。翻唱R010R的《Bloodsucker》以暗色EBM重构。整体而言，这是一张扎实稳健的old-school EBM制作，制作精良，对该类型爱好者而言值得一听。

items.body: Vampire Valentine, the darkwave and post-punk duo from Newcastle upon Tyne, release their self-titled debut album “Vampire Valentine” on Morella Records on 28 August 2026. The record runs to 16 tracks and 78 minutes, and comes out on digital platforms and on CD. The album closes a year that began with a signature. Vampire Valentine signed to Morella Records on 15 January 2026 as the label’s first act, a date Morella now marks as its own founding anniversary. Michael Longstaff handles vocals and co-production, Kieron Wright plays bass and guitar, and US producer Ricky Conover supplies the synth and instrumental work that runs between the songs. Tony Gunk and label founder Blake Carpenter also produced, with Carpenter contributing guitar and handling mixing and mastering. The duo bring angular guitars, driving bass and vocals pitched between melody and unease, mixing post-punk urgency with gothic atmosphere, cyberpunk ambience and 1980s synth work. Five singles ran ahead of the album across 2026: “Tears” on 14 February and “Skin” on 27 March, then three drawn from the album itself, “In The Dark” on 19 June, “Cutting Ties” on 24 July and “Another Day” on 7 August. Longstaff describes the record as an unedited version of the band rather than a polished one. “We didn’t set out to make something comfortable. Every song on this record came from somewhere real, and we weren’t interested in softening any of it. This is us, completely, for the first time at full length.” Carpenter explains why the album was worth building the label around. “Vampire Valentine were the first artists to sign to Morella Records, and this album is exactly why. There was no hedging in what they were, not from the very first conversation. You can hear it in this record: The Cure, Bauhaus, all of it filtered through a band that already knew exactly who they are, finally given the room to say all of it at once.” VAMPIRE VALENTINE by Vampire Valentine Vampire Valentine’s debut album: the 16 tracks “Suffocation” “In The Dark” “Cutting Ties” “August Heat” “Imperfect” “The Other Side” “Empty Heart Heavy Eyes” “You Weren’t There For Me” “Obelisk” “Another Day” “Resurrect” “Don’t Talk About It” “Forsaken” “Black Sky” “Final Breath” “Lovesong (The Cure Cover)” Six of the sixteen tracks are instrumentals, most of them Conover’s. “August Heat”, “The Other Side”, “Obelisk”, “Forsaken”, “Black Sky” and “Final Breath” break up the vocal songs, with “The Other Side” reworking the chord progression of “Imperfect” at a faster tempo and “Final Breath” closing the record on ambient synth. Longstaff has said the closer brings survival horror games such as Resident Evil and Silent Hill to mind. Among the vocal tracks, “Resurrect” is the band’s tribute to Bauhaus, built around the idea of being undead, and takes Longstaff’s delivery to its harshest point on the record. “You Weren’t There For Me” is the song he has called the one he is most personally tied to, though he has not said who it is about. The Cure cover “Lovesong” closes the running order and is exclusive to the Bandcamp edition. The album is available on all digital platforms and as a deluxe CD shipping from the UK through the Morella Records store and the band’s Bandcamp page. About Vampire Valentine Vampire Valentine formed in October 2025 in Newcastle upon Tyne, founded by singer and producer Michael Longstaff and bassist and guitarist Kieron Wright. The duo cite The Sisters of Mercy and Twin Tribes among their reference points, and mix gothic rock, post-punk and darkwave with synth work from US producer Ricky Conover, who records as Forerunnerx. Their first releases came out on their own Bandcamp page: the single “Porcelain” on 14 November 2025, followed by an instrumental edition, and “Thorns” on 1 December 2025. On 15 January 2026 they signed to Morella Records, the independent label founded that same month by Blake Carpenter and based in Georgia in the United States, with a roster covering goth rock, deathrock, darkwave and post-punk. Vampire Valentine were the label’s first signing. The year that followed produced the album “Dry Remains” on 14 January 2026, the “Pale Dawn” EP on 17 April, and the five singles that led into the debut. Side-Line covered the run as it went out, from “In The Dark” through the “Cutting Ties” single to the album announcement in June, when the release still carried no exact date. The self-titled album gathers that year into one 78-minute record and is the duo’s first full-length under the Morella name.
