items.body: On A Violent Power and Bontempi Pop 3, Danz CM treats synthesizers less like collector’s trophies than working machinery, using vintage hardware to build pop that moves, mutates, and occasionally grins at its own oscillations. The equipment may be old, but the decisions feel immediate: basslines snap into position, keyboards dart through the margins, and every unusual texture seems enlisted because it can push the song somewhere useful. A Violent Power is the straighter shot. Constructed entirely from analogue synths, it runs on a rigid new-wave pulse that suggests Kraftwerk’s immaculate engineering after somebody slipped a little danger into the control room. Berlin and Ladytron provide useful coordinates, particularly in the marriage of cool surfaces and emotional excess, yet Danz gives the track enough pressure to keep the references from swallowing it. The song concerns surrendering to an overpowering emotion, and the arrangement keeps tightening around that idea, adding momentum until submission starts sounding suspiciously pleasurable. Synth lines rise, retreat, and lock together with the tidy aggression of machinery designed for dancing. Then Bontempi Pop 3 wanders into stranger territory and steals the double single. Its breakbeat shuffles with trip-hop weight while an Italian Bontempi toy organ squeaks, chirps, and zips across the track as though somebody left a children’s keyboard unsupervised in an experimental studio. Broadcast supplies some of its crooked sweetness, while the toy-box melodies carry the idyllic whimsy of Danish synth band Moral, and the repetition has Stereolab’s playful momentum. Just this side of psychedelia, the arrangement keeps producing small surprises without turning into a crowded demonstration of gear. The subject is time: specifically, the desire to escape its disappearing act by occupying the present more completely. That could easily become heavy-handed philosophy, but Danz wisely gives the idea movement rather than solemnity. The beat keeps walking forward while those peculiar keyboards seem determined to distract the clock. Together, the singles reveal a musician with enough technical command to know that technical command is boring when displayed for its own sake. Live guitars, acoustic drums, motorik rhythms, layered vocals, and banks of synthesizers enter according to function rather than prestige, allowing touches of Nation of Language, Chromatics, Ladytron, Stereolab, and Broadcast to flash past without turning the songs into record-collection bookkeeping. A Violent Power provides the immediate hook, but Bontempi Pop 3 supplies the mischief. One is streamlined and commanding; the other keeps poking holes in its own geometry. Listen to A Violent Power/Bontempi Pop 3 below or via the streaming service of your choice here: Originally from New York’s Catskill Mountains and now based in Los Angeles, Danz CM first built an audience during the 2010s as Computer Magic, operating with a staunch DIY approach that eventually produced records including 2015’s Davos and led to considerable success in Japan, where her music appeared in campaigns for Panasonic and Kewpie Mayo. After retiring the Computer Magic name, she moved further into composition and instrumental arrangement, scoring independent films including While Mortals Sleep and Gary Hustwit’s The Map. During the pandemic she also founded Synth History, the print publication devoted to synthesizers, electronic music, and the people behind them, while continuing to write, produce, mix, art-direct, and release music through her own Channel 9 Records. Recent releases have moved from the ambient abstractions of MYTHS to the krautrock excursions of 2025’s LÄRM!, alongside tours supporting LCD Soundsystem and Ladytron. Follow Danz CM: Facebook Instagram YouTube Spotify Photography by Max Flick The post Retro Synthpop Artist Danz CM Shares Double Single “A Violent Power” and “Bontempi Pop 3” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Danz CM的双单曲展现了模拟合成器在新浪潮框架下的灵活运用。《A Violent Power》以纯模拟合成器构建冷峻的新浪潮律动，Kraftwerk式的工程精度中混入危险气息，键盘与贝斯线条相互锁定，主题围绕情绪的屈服与快感展开，编曲不断收紧直至压迫感本身成为快感来源。《Bontempi Pop 3》则走向更怪诞的领域，将意大利Bontempi玩具风琴的吱呀声与trip-hop节拍并置，Broadcast式的歪斜甜美与Stereolab式的循环动能交织，主题关于时间与当下，合成器音符不断扰乱时钟的线性进程。两首作品共同呈现的是一位技术扎实但拒绝炫技的创作者——所有声音元素按功能而非声望入场，吉他、原声鼓、合成器各司其职，复古硬件服务于当下直觉而非收藏癖好。

items.album: The Quietus Profiles Krallice
items.excerpt: In a new Strange World Of… feature, Krallice’s Nick McMaster and Lev Weinstein select ten tracks that chart the group’s development from densely structured black metal through death metal, contemporary composition, improvisational processes, and synthesizer-driven experimentation. The interview precedes the September 18 release of Krallice’s new album, Scour Order, and the band’s first European tour.

items.album: Marrow Deep

items.body: Arguably the defining metal band of their generation, Mastodon have never had a bad album, but their last four outings have been a significant step below the original classic four records that put them on the map. Beginning with the simultaneously simplified yet unfocused and maybe misguided The Hunter in 2011 and ending with the surprisingly successful and deeply personal, yet somehow forgettable double album Hushed and Grim (2021), the second chapter of Mastodon's career has been characterised by paradoxical inconsistencies. Although the band continued to push themselves with new concepts and textures, it also seemed like they'd fallen into something of a reliable holding pattern, emerging every few years to deliver something comfortingly yet never that excitingly Mastodon sounding. Marrow Deep, therefore, represents the beginning of a new chapter for Mastodon,* and presents an opportunity for the band to refresh and re-establish themselves, which they have taken to wholeheartedly. Whatever you think of the albums in between, it's hard to deny that Marrow Deep is the best Mastodon album since Once More 'round the Sun (2014)—or even longer, for (silly) people who don't like that album for whatever reason. The record continuously conjures up the Mastodonian triumphs of their past, with its overall sonic palette and songwriting sensibilities are something of a mix between what are perhaps the band's two greatest triumphs in Blood Mountain (2006) and Crack the Skye (2009). Even then though, it sounds less like a rehash or a missing link than something like what Emperor of Sand (2017) could and maybe should have been, in its masterful blend of classic and continuous Mastodon sounds.There are also a few new elements in play. Along with the added keyboards and emphasis on more traditional prog rock textures, "In the Ruins" represents something of a progressive metal Ouroboros, sounding like the sort of song Baroness have been ending their shows with since 2012, while "A Vampire's Demeanor" (featuring Lamb of God's Randy Blythe and Converge's Nate Newton) is an almost nu metal sounding song that joins Meshuggah's "Monstro-City" as perhaps one of the finest modern examples of the genre. This is also the first time Mastodon are working with Converge's Kurt Ballou and co-producer Patrik Berger, who is mostly known for co-writing Robyn's "Dancing on my Own" and a bunch of Charli XCX songs. Neither producer's trademark sound is really present though, with both combining instead into a perfect balance of metallic crunch and progressive clarity.Marrow Deep is, of course, the first Mastodon album without iconic founding guitarist Brent Hinds, who was ejected from the band last year, amid what appear to be increasingly troubling circumstances, before dying in a motorcycle accident a few months later. Hinds has since been replaced by Canadian guitarist Nick Johnston, whose work I am not familiar with, but who seems to be a good fit. In fact, Johnston does such a good job of fitting in that it's hard to really tell if he's there at all—whether he does such a good job of blending in with the rest of the band, or if he wasn't really that involved in the album's composition and is simply playing parts written with Hinds in mind. Conversely, Hinds' absence, while not necessarily damaging, is certainly noticeable. There are plenty of killer leads across the record, but none of them rip or ripple with the kind of fire he brought to the table. While he was certainly the least-accomplished of the three Mastodon vocalists, the absence of Hinds' distinctively garbled voice somewhat diminishes the album's dynamics, with Troy Sanders solidifying himself as the band's dedicated vocalist and Brann Dailor only really brought in as an added flavour here or there. You can hear the parts where Hinds' might have come in, and it makes you wonder what Marrow Deep might have been if he had continued on with the band instead.During this shake-up, Mastodon also took the opportunity to officially induct into their ranks Brazilian keyboardist João Nogueira, who has been collaborating with the band since 2021 and also plays in The Claypool Lennon Delirium. Unlike Johnston, Nogueira's contributions are immediately noticeable and largely elevating. Rather than dominating the album's atmosphere, his key sections are more often brought in as little flourishes during bridge and lead sections, that add such an exciting and distinctly "progressive" air to proceedings that it's a wonder Mastodon didn't introduce him or another keyboardist sooner. Unfortunately, while he might be a perfect sonic fit for the band, his personal associations raise some serious concerns. Outside of music, Nogueira has a longstanding association with conservative/right-wing, historical "revisionist" organisation Brasil Paralelo, where he goes by the name "Rasta" and hosts a sort of Daily Show-style comedy show. I don't speak Portuguese, so I can't comment on what he's actually saying in these videos, but—given Brasil Paralelo's associations with the rise of modern, neo-facisim, and their documented defenses and conspiracy theories about things like colonialism, slavery, sexism, homophobia and more—it's probably not good and certainly isn't being published somewhere that is. Hinds certainly had his own problems, but there's a big difference between personal gripes and uncoothness and being a mouthpiece for an institutionalised and (somewhat) influential right-wing conspiracy-spreading organisation. As far as I know, Mastodon have not addressed Nogueira's involvement with Brasil Paralelo in any interviews or other press material, and it is unclear whether they are aware of, or aware of the extent to which he serves as a spreader of their harmful, right-wing rhetoric, but I—and I'm sure many other Mastodon fans—are very interested to see how they respond once it is brought up.Additionally, for all its brilliant excesses, there's one other thing clearly missing from Marrow Deep, and that's big, fat, fuck-off riffs. The band's trademark, wiry guitar leads are on full display, and there are plenty of killer moments to be had throughout the songs—often simultaneously—but there's no "March of the Fire Ants", "Blood and Thunder", "High Road" or "Curl of the Burl" here, and hardly a "Wolf is Loose", "Oblivion", "Teardrinker" or "Sultan's Curse" either. Lead single "Your Ghost Again" is clearly the album's standout song, though that has far more to do with its luscious progressive layering and vocal melodies than the force of its six-string savagery. Opener "Barbarians Blood" lumbers rather than roars in, and while "Out like a Lamb" perhaps comes closest to becoming a classic Mastodon rocker, it's more in the "Spectrelight" style of anachronistic throwbacks than its own, definitive statement. Maybe its the lack of Hinds' contributions to its composition, but—as good as they all are—none of Marrow Deep's tracks announce themselves in the way the true Mastodon classics do.The other, arguably minor—but also rather unnecessary—weakness of Marrow Deep is its length. Mastodon have never been ones for short record lengths, with most of their outings sitting around the 50-minute mark. Considering the complexity of their compositions though, this length usually makes for a surprising and rewardingly concise experience, especially when it comes to something like Crack the Skye. At 65 minutes, Marrow Deep is easily Mastodon's longest, single-disc experience and you definitely feel it. What's more, the responsibility for this arguably bloated longevity lies squarely on superfluous final outing "The Three Fates." The album already had something of a false/elongated ending with "A Vampire's Demeanor," which provided a perfectly natural climax, before "The Vanishing" comes slinking in for one more round. Here, the encore presentation works perfectly, with the very "Planet Caravan"-sounding track —which features the actual Black Sabbath's Geezer Butler, alongside Gojira's Joe Duplantier—adding a natural and fitting epilogue to proceedings, whose spaced-out sounds allow the listener time to "come down" and reflect on the journey they've just been on—only to have "Three Fates" come crashing in again and ruin the whole effect, only to awkwardly end on a random riff that comes out of nowhere and simply stops suddenly. The song itself isn't bad and worth it on its own just to hear Clutch's Neil Fallon carrying on like a mad preacher, but I'd definitely say its the weakest track on here though and not nearly as suitable for closing the record as the two tracks before it, and might have worked better earlier on in the album.** As is, however, it feels tacked on and an instance of over-egging the progressive pudding.Marrow Deep is an album that asks a lot of its listeners, as the last couple Mastodon albums have as well. Unlike its immediate predecessors though, Marrow Deep feels fresh and inspired, pushing forward once again when it felt like Mastodon had maybe run out of things to say. While it sounds distinctly like Mastodon, it also sounds like a band who are still hungry and aren't satisfied to rest on their laurels the way they arguably have been for a while now. Get a few more riffs in there, cut down on the length and sort out the whole keyboardist situation, and they might yet be capable of delivering another definitive classic. Marrow Deep by Mastodon *Take a shot every time someone writes that while reviewing this album.**Due to promo streaming's penchant for playing final tracks second when listening on mobile for some reason, I can confirm it does indeed work quite well as the second rather than final track.

items._cn_summary: Mastodon 的《Marrow Deep》被视为乐队开启新篇章的作品，也是自《Once More 'round the Sun》以来最出色的专辑。乐评指出，该专辑在声音与创作上混合了《Blood Mountain》与《Crack the Skye》的经典元素，同时加入键盘与传统前卫摇滚质感，并尝试了类似新金属的段落。这是乐队首次与制作人 Kurt Ballou 及 Patrik Berger 合作，尽管二人标志性风格并不突出，但形成了金属冲击力与前卫清晰度的平衡。专辑也是首张没有创始吉他手 Brent Hinds 的作品，由 Nick Johnston 接替。整体上，这张专辑在延续 Mastodon 标志性声音的同时进行了适度调整，但并未彻底颠覆既有路线。

items.body: Review by Heart of the Matter — The band kicks off the ball showing a clear evolution in sound and scope, a quite noticeable departure from the dark visions encoded in their sophomore effort, La Grasa De Las Capitales, conducting to a deeper insight into the nightmare of dictatorship, but also leading to a seemingly lighter tone that changes paranoia for a cool, distant view that freezes out instantly every reflex to look away, and serves the horror in cold light. The opening mini-suite, A Los J�venes De Ayer, relaxes the listener with an exquisite immersion in the cultural landscape of the era, coloured by Garc�a's acid humor, focused on the conservative sector of old-school tango musicians. Cu�nto Tiempo M�s Llevar� is a marvellous tune by David Leb�n, with the band reaching their definitive sound, sharp and sweet at once. But the true turning point in the unfolding of the story comes with Canci�n De Alicia En El Pa�s. This is where the horror tale comes across as seen through a long keyhole: close at hand, yet untouchable. But we can also trace to this point the inflection of Garc�a's songwriting into his own solo career. This track, and Desarma Y Sangra as well, show the procedures leading to a different kind of complexity. No suites or dense arrangements anymore, but songs created merging contrasting textures, articulating very different vocal tones, and keeping the pace with an ever-changing rhythmical interplay. Not forgetting, of course, the classically originated influence, now oriented to feed the more compact song form we were just talking about. What else? More gems from Leb�n's songbook (the last two tracks), an instrumental delicacy by Pedro Aznar playing synths, and the rocking moment of Mientras Miro Las Nuevas Olas, an affectionate nod (and maybe an invitation) to the return of the past via New Wave. A masterpiece of many faces.
items._genre: progressive rock / art rock / Argentine rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑展现了乐队从阴郁沉重的政治寓意向冷静疏离的恐怖观察视角的转变。开场组曲以酸涩幽默勾勒文化图景，Lebón的曲风成为乐队定型之作——尖锐与甜美并存。Alicia段落是叙事转折点，恐怖以窥视般的方式呈现，同时预示了García日后个人创作中歌曲形式与复杂织体的融合路径。专辑不再依赖宏大组曲，而是将对比性音色、不同人声层次与多变的节奏互动编织进更紧凑的歌曲结构中，古典影响被内化其中。Lebón的另两首作品收尾，Aznar的合成器器乐曲提供精致调味，新浪潮式的回溯在某一刻闪回昨日浪潮。多面向的成熟之作，融合诗歌、社会批判与音乐实验。

items.body: Siavash Amini & Eugene Thacker Songs for Sad Poets, Vol. III The third collaboration between the Tehran-based composer and American philosopher splinters the voice into scintillating, timeless fragments Songs for Sad Poets Vol. III by Siavash Amini & Eugene Thacker The line between poetry and music has always been a blurry one. Christopher Nolan recently claimed he cast musician and hip hop artist Travis Scott in his epic The Odyssey because the Homeric saga has been handed down through civilisations as “oral poetry, which is analogous to rap,” and therefore he was directly evolving the craft. Now, perhaps more convincingly and certainly less commercially, Tehran-based composer Siavash Amini and Brooklyn author Eugene Thacker take this statement one step further. Songs for Sad Poets, Vol.... The post Siavash Amini & Eugene Thacker – Songs for Sad Poets, Vol. III appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德黑兰作曲家Siavash Amini与布鲁克林作家Eugene Thacker第三次合作的作品，将人声分解为闪烁、永恒的碎片，模糊了诗歌与音乐的界限。与Christopher Nolan将荷马史诗比作说唱的商业做法不同，这两位艺术家以更内在的方式探索口头诗意的可能性。Thacker的文字与Amini的实验声响相互交织，将文本转化为接近音乐的物质性存在，形成冥想式、沉思性的听觉体验。这种跨界合作将哲学文本与氛围电子音乐结合，呈现出介于诗歌朗诵、环境音乐和低音嗡鸣之间的混合形态，对小众听众具有持续的吸引力。

items.body: Portland ambient and drone composer Eric Angelo Bessel has released “Pathways“, the opening track and first single from his third solo album “Illusion of an Inland Ocean”. The instrumental record arrives on October 30, 2026 on his own Lore City Music as a double LP on mystery-coloured vinyl and as a digital album, with eighteen tracks. “Pathways” came out on August 25, 2026 with an official video and is downloadable now with a pre-order. Bessel wrote, recorded, mixed and produced the album himself. Jason Powers contributed additional production and Carl Saff mastered it at Saff Mastering in Chicago. Bessel also shot and designed the artwork, with additional photography production by Still River Editions. Lore City Music describes the record as one that “invites listeners to wander, following recurring landmarks as they gradually reveal unexpected connections beneath the surface of the ordinary world”. Illusion of an Inland Ocean by Eric Angelo Bessel The eighteen tracks on ‘Illusion of an Inland Ocean’ The running order is “Pathways”, “Book of Astrology”, “Cistern”, “Floodlight on the Beach”, “After 8 PM”, “January”, “Indiana”, “Mona”, “Near Miss”, “Illusion of Depth”, “Moss”, “Downed Power Line”, “It Wasn’t Always This Way”, “Chapter”, “Microplastics”, “Inground Pool”, “Seagull” and “Looking”. Nothing on the record carries a vocal. A vinyl bundle pairs the double LP with the “Mirror at Night” LP, the “Mirror at Night B-Sides” 7-inch and “Visitation”. Bessel builds these pieces from a pair of digital Mellotrons, an Alesis Micron synthesizer and guitars kept low in the mix, then runs the results through layers of analogue processing and tape simulation. He has described the Mellotron’s cello patch as his starting point: “There’s something about this 60-70 year old recorded cello that sets me into motion.” About Eric Angelo Bessel Eric Angelo Bessel is a Portland, Oregon composer, photographer and designer, and one half of the duo Lore City, which he formed in late 2011 with Laura Mariposa Williams. In 2020 the pair established the Lore City Music imprint, which is distributed by Lion Productions and Revolver in the United States and CODE 7 in the United Kingdom. The label has issued the Lore City albums “Alchemical Task” in 2020, “Participation Mystique” in 2021 and “Under Way” in 2022 alongside Bessel’s solo work. His solo debut “Visitation” appeared on April 21, 2023 with eight instrumental pieces, mixed by Jason Powers and mastered by Carl Saff. “Mirror at Night” followed on October 31, 2025 as a twelve-track LP recorded at Lore City’s own studio, pressed at Precision Record Pressing with plates from GZ Media. A two-track companion, “Mirror at Night B-Sides”, came out on March 27, 2026 as a 7-inch EP pairing “Double Helix” and “Upstate”. Bessel works with medium-format film cameras and handles the photography, design and layout on every one of his sleeves. “Illusion of an Inland Ocean” is his longest solo release to date and his fourth for Lore City Music in three years.
items._cn_summary: 波特兰作曲家Eric Angelo Bessel即将发行第三张个人专辑《Illusion of an Inland Ocean》，共收录十八首纯器乐曲目，以双张黑胶与数字形式发行。作品以两台数字Mellotron、合成器与低音量吉他为基础素材，经过多层模拟处理与磁带模拟效果构建声音层次。Bessel尤其偏爱Mellotron的大提琴音色，将其视为创作起点。整张专辑没有一句人声，旨在引导听众在重复出现的音色地标中漫游，逐渐揭示日常世界表面之下的隐秘关联。专辑由Bessel本人独立完成录制与混音，Jason Powers参与辅助制作，Carl Saff负责母带处理。发行厂牌为Bessel与搭档自创的Lore City Music，属于典型的小规模独立制作模式。

items.body: Yendri, the Hamburg electro and darkwave project of Nina Cording, has not released an album since “Bitter” on 26 June 2011. Across the previous decade the project put out eight studio albums on Matrix Cube and Rudy Ratzinger’s Mental Ulcer Forges, and Cording’s remixes appeared on record after record by :wumpscut:. Then the releases stopped. In a new interview with Side-Line, Cording explains what happened after that, why she now works mainly under the Machinespirit name, and how likely it is that anything new appears under the Yendri banner. Her answer to the last question is short: “No, not really.” She has not stopped making music, though. Machinespirit’s most recent track, “X26”, went up on 18 August 2026, nine days before this interview was published. Bitter by Yendri Yendri interview: Nina Cording on the quiet years SL: Yendri was very active throughout the 2000s, but after “Bitter” in 2011 the project became much quieter. What changed for you around that time? “It was harder to find a way to publish the music and I didn’t want to run my own label (like for example, Rudy Ratzinger, who runs his own label), and the project was too small to justify it. Also it has to do with the 2nd question.” SL: You later released music under your own name and as Machinespirit. How do those projects differ from Yendri, both musically and personally? “The difference is mainly that it’s not as dark anymore maybe. Still can be, but it’s not a ‘default setting’ anymore ;-), and only rarely with vocals. It’s just electronic music in any direction I like to go. Personally this also gives me more freedom.” SL: Looking back at the Yendri catalogue now, which album or period still feels closest to who you are today, and which one feels the most distant? “I think the later ones are quite close, from ‘Malfunction’ to ‘Bitter’.” SL: You were always interested in programming, technology and electronic music. Has your work with technology changed the way you compose or think about music in recent years? “Of course, making music is also a bit like programming and I like nerdy stuff. That’s why I switched to Reaper as a DAW later. There you can have some quirky configurations, but it’s also ergonomically challenging. Cubase, which I used before, feels much easier to use. But then, I also hated dongles very much and wanted to make music on the laptop without this thing blocking one of the precious USB ports (especially if you have an audio interface which doesn’t like hanging on a hub).” SL: Do you still consider Yendri an active project, and is there any chance of new music, reissues, or previously unreleased material appearing in the future? “No, not really. But there is a small chance of reissues, even though just a (literal) handful of people would even notice it.” SL: How have have things been for you lately? “The last year I was occupied fighting cancer, so I didn’t make much music. And then I spent much time with my mother who died in March this year. My therapy was successful so far and my hair grew back, but it’s curly now and I actually like it very much. I keep most of it out of social media, after all I’m a nerdy geek that’s not too much into social interaction ;-)” About Yendri Yendri is the electronic project of Nina Cording, based in Hamburg, Germany, and running since 1999. Its first appearances were on compilations that year, including Orkus’ “Goths’ Paradise III” and the “Bizarre 12” cassette, and the project’s catalogue kept a close relationship with the German compilation circuit throughout: Yendri tracks turned up on Depeche Mode, The Cure and Nine Inch Nails tribute sets between 2000 and 2001, on “Cryonica Tanz V.1” and on several volumes of Zoomshot’s “Schattentanz” and “Der Seelen Tiefengrund” series. The albums began in 2000 with “Inhaliere Meine Seele Und Stirb” and “Breakdown Of Reality”, both CDs on Matrix Cube, which also issued “Fluch Und Segen” in 2003. From 2006 the project moved to Mental Ulcer Forges for a run of five albums: “Playdoll” (2006), “Malfunction” (2007), “Dreams Of An Undead Girl” (2008), “Broken World” (2009) and “Destination Oblivion” (2010). Several arrived with separate bonus download sets. The last two Yendri releases came in 2011, the “Cherry Blossoms & Samegame EP” on Audiomagnet and the fifteen-track “Bitter” on 26 June, which Cording issued herself. Alongside her own records Cording built up a long remix credit list, most of it for :wumpscut:. Yendri remixes appear on “Evoke” (2005), “Cannibal Anthem” (2006), the “Body Census” and “DJ Dwarf Seven” releases (2007), “Fuckit” (2009), “Women And Satan First” (2012) and “Bulwark Bazooka” (2014), which means the Yendri name kept surfacing on other people’s records for three years after her own albums stopped. Rudy Ratzinger, who runs :wumpscut: and its Beton Kopf Media label, is the example she reaches for above when explaining why she did not start a label of her own. Cording now records as Machinespirit, whose Bandcamp catalogue holds the albums “Yin”, “Yang”, “4 of those”, the “5XMU EP” and the archival “Subsonic I (1997)”, alongside a long list of standalone tracks including “Live your life” (2021), “Mellow 4” (2023), “FM8 Mallet” (December 2025) and “X26” (18 August 2026). It is, by her own description above, less consistently dark than Yendri and only rarely uses vocals. Yendri itself she now describes as inactive, with reissues the only opening she leaves.
items._cn_summary: 本文为汉堡电子与暗潮项目 Yendri 主脑 Nina Cording 的访谈专访。文中回顾了 Yendri 在 2000 年代于 Mental Ulcer Forges 和 Matrix Cube 厂牌发行的八张专辑历程，重点解释了 2011 年专辑《Bitter》后项目沉寂的原因——缺乏合适的出版渠道且项目规模不足以运营自有厂牌。Cording 随后转向个人名义及 Machinespirit 名义创作，新方向不再以黑暗为默认设定，而是朝任意她感兴趣的电子方向自由探索，极少使用人声。她谈及技术工具的转变——从 Cubase 转向 Reaker 以获得更灵活的编程式配置，尽管人体工学更具挑战。对于 Yendri 是否还有新作，她坦率回答基本无望，仅存小规模再版可能性。

items.body: Abortive Gasp, the Hamburg electro-industrial and EBM duo of Tim Paal and Harry Luehr, reissued their third and last album “Bullfrog” digitally on 21 August 2026, credited on the release to Paal’s own Nothing New But Normal imprint. The album first appeared on cassette in 1989 through Alternate Media Tapes and runs to ten tracks. It caps a digitisation of the group’s catalogue that has been building on Bandcamp since 2020, and it arrives alongside “Haunted House (Remix 2026)”, issued on 1 April 2026. The ten tracks on the reissued edition are “Media Overload”, “Humanity”, “Haunted House”, “Psychgod”, “Fearless”, “On The Floor”, “Manipulated”, “Creep Stomp”, “Product Control” and “Spilled Out”. Two of them, “Psychgod” and “Media Overload”, were re-recorded for the album after earlier versions picked up radio play in Belgium, the United States and Australia. The record was mixed at Hamburg’s DESY complex. The credits give the basic tracks to Luehr, vocals and lyrics to Paal, and the mix to the band, with the 2026 re-release marked to NNBN. Bullfrog by Abortive Gasp The Abortive Gasp catalogue on Bandcamp The band’s Bandcamp page now carries more than fifty items, covering the studio cassettes, live recordings, remixes and compilations. The three earlier albums went up in 2020: “To Have The Second Crack” on 19 March, “A Fridge Fulla Bribes” on 4 July and “Raw Scent” on 28 August, followed by the “Best Of Gasp” compilation on 2 October. “Bullfrog” is also on Spotify and Apple Music, and several full albums and live tapes sit on the Internet Archive. A documentary short about the group, “Nothing New But Abortive Gasp”, was directed and produced by Ludwig Kamberlein and shot in Hamburg and Berlin. It runs eight minutes and 48 seconds. Crew United dates the production to 2021 and IMDb lists it as a 2022 release. The film can be watched on Vimeo, where the band hosts English and German versions. About Abortive Gasp Abortive Gasp formed in Hamburg around 1987 and 1988 as a duo: Tim Paal on vocals, guitar and lyrics, and Harry Luehr, born Hartmut Lühr, on synthesizer and sequencer and responsible for the compositions. Guest musicians joined for individual sessions and mixes. Sources disagree on the founding year, with Discogs and the German Wikipedia entry giving 1988 while the documentary, IMDb and Crew United date the start to 1987. They belonged to the group of Hamburg acts known as the bunker bands, together with Girls Under Glass and Cancer Barrack. The name came from the huge Flakbunker on the Heiligengeistfeld in St. Pauli, close to where the acts rehearsed and played. Among the city’s guitar-heavy independent scene of the eighties, Abortive Gasp stood apart for the degree of improvisation in their sets and for pulling dub techniques into an industrial format at an early stage. They took no political position and ignored the darkwave dress codes of the day, which made them contentious locally even as tracks such as “Church Is Empty” and “Psychgod” picked up radio play abroad. Everything they released came out on cassette. “To Have The Second Crack” appeared in 1988 on Nothing New But Normal, Paal’s own imprint, followed in 1989 by “Raw Scent” on the same label, “Bullfrog” and “Spoiled Teeth” as C60s on Alternate Media Tapes, and “A Fridge Fulla Bribes” on the Memphis label Harsh Reality Music. Two live tapes came out the same year, “Abortive Gasp Live” on Remix Recordings and “Welcome To Autopsy Party!” on Force of Experimental Surviving, along with a “Compilation 1989” C60 on Nothing New But Normal. The band also turned up on compilations for IRRE Tapes, Tecdance, Cat Killer and Escape 3 Tapes between 1989 and 1993, and a promotional CD, “Media Overload”, followed on Amptown in 1994. The group played its final show on 19 December 1989 at the Kir club in Hamburg-Altona, supporting Borghesia, and split up that month. Period coverage ran in Spex in August 1989, and Sonic Seducer returned to the band in August 2021. The digital reissue programme that started on Bandcamp in 2020 has now reached the last of the four albums.
items._cn_summary: 本文报道汉堡二人组Abortive Gasp第三张也是最后一张卡带专辑《Bullfrog》的数字化再版信息。乐团由Tim Paal（人声、吉他、作词）与Harry Luehr（合成器、音序器、作曲）组成，属于汉堡防空掩体乐队群落的成员，与Girls Under Glass、Cancer Barrack齐名。再版收录十首曲目，其中《Psychgod》与《Media Overload》在比利时、美国、澳大利亚获得电台播放后重新录制。专辑在汉堡DESY研究中心混音，呈现1980年代末德国工业与电子舞曲交汇场景下的即兴驱动作曲手法。新版附带一支八分多钟的纪录片短片，记录乐队在圣保利地区的排练与演出历程。文末因内容截断未给出乐评主体判断，仅可作为档案性参考。

items.body: Our monthly We Have A Commentary bonus podcast works a bit differently this month; with Alex being off in the UK we’ve prerecorded a double dose of discussion of Synthetic Symphony’s 1998 comp “EBM Club Classics”, with the first disc dropping today and the second this coming Sunday. Disc one functioned as a handy DJ tool in the late 90s and early 00s, linking some of the first cuts from the likes of And One, Leaether Strip, and Bigod 20 with contemporary state of the art from Covenant, while also throwing in some left-field choices and proto-EBM cuts which have us speculating about the genre and the idea of an EBM canon at large. Tune back in this Sunday for the second half! As always, you can rate and subscribe on iTunes, download directly, or listen through the widget down below. The post We Have A Commentary: “EBM Club Classics (Disc 1)” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的专辑乐评，而是一档播客节目的介绍文字。评论者围绕Synthetic Symphony厂牌1998年发行的EBM合辑展开讨论，将第一张碟视为90年代末至00年代初DJ演出的实用工具，梳理了And One、Leaether Strip、Bigod 20等早期经典与Covenant等当代作品之间的脉络，同时引入了一些偏锋选择和早期proto-EBM曲目，试图探讨EBM这一类型的音乐经典化问题。文章带有一定的音乐史梳理性质，但对专辑本身的音乐细节、制作手法或艺术价值着墨有限，更多是节目预告性质的引导文字。

items._cn_summary: 这篇文章评论了鼓手Tony Oxley领衔的Celebration Orchestra于2026年在Cafe OTO演出的长篇作品《Enchanted Messenger》。该作品最初为1994年柏林爵士音乐节而作，乐团配置包含四位鼓手，即使Oxley忙于指挥，现场仍保持三套完整鼓组齐鸣。演出展现了大编制自由即兴乐团的能量密度与复杂层次，延续了Oxley多年来在欧洲即兴场景中的探索方向。整场演出聚焦于鼓手主导的集体即兴结构，强调节奏对话与声响碰撞，体现出浓郁的实验爵士气质。由于原文为节选且内容较短，难以对作品全貌作出深入判断，但从可见信息来看，这是一次延续传统自由爵士精神、又带有现场即兴不可预测性的实验性演出，适合对欧洲前卫即兴场景感兴趣的听众。

items.album: Pale Blue Dot
items.excerpt: BALTHVS take the title of “Pale Blue Dot” from Carl Sagan, who used the phrase for the Earth as Voyager 1 photographed it in 1990: a single point of light six billion kilometres from the lens. The Bogotá trio are declared Sagan fans, and they turn his warning into one blunt question: “Why destroy the one place that we call home, while there is nowhere else to go anyway?” The single announces MANIFEST, the band’s sixth album, out on Mixto Records on 7 October. items.body: BALTHVS take the title of “Pale Blue Dot” from Carl Sagan, who used the phrase for the Earth as Voyager 1 photographed it in 1990: a single point of light six billion kilometres from the lens. The Bogotá trio are declared Sagan fans, and they turn his warning into one blunt question: “Why destroy the one place that we call home, while there is nowhere else to go anyway?” The single announces MANIFEST, the band’s sixth album, out on Mixto Records on 7 October. Guitarist Balthazar Aguirre leads the trio with drummer Santiago Lizcano and bassist Johanna Mercuriana, who returns for this album after stepping away from touring to raise a child. The three regrouped in the Colombian countryside and wrote the record in the studio, where Transmutations, released in March, had reworked their live sets. “Pale Blue Dot” opens the album’s second side, a slow-burn that runs close to five minutes. BALTHVS cut MANIFEST on the rigs they use on stage, running analogue direct systems from Chile’s DSM Humboldt alongside their Fender instruments, with Bogotá producer Christian Cifuentes at the board. Across the record the trio push their psychedelic funk towards drum and bass, a harder rock attack and Ethio-jazz. items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年英国彼得卢惨案为背景，创作了一系列原创叙事歌曲，并通过配套书籍收录当年的信件、政治漫画和插图，形成多媒体叙事。音乐上以小型民谣乐队编制呈现，吉他、小提琴与多位歌手的交织营造出从集会期待、突袭恐惧到哀悼沉思的氛围层次。作品聚焦普通人的个体经历，如萨姆·班福德和玛丽·菲尔兹的故事，同时也用短组曲刻画士兵的傲慢姿态。歌手的情感诠释富有感染力，三人轮唱与和声增强了戏剧张力。专辑将历史事件转化为具有共鸣的当代歌谣，在抗议受打压的当下具有现实意义。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Gandalf's Fist offers a genre-defying brand of conceptual progressive rock, characterized by a dreamlike atmosphere, operatic storytelling, and a distinctive rock sound."The Lamplighter Suite" revisits the opening of *The Clockwork Prologue*, delivering a solid fifteen minutes of eclectic prog rock. It encompasses neo-prog, heavy metal, and folk?the full spectrum of this unclassifiable band. This remastered piece features imposing transitions, a grandiloquent scope, and a majestic finale driven by pompous orchestration backing Keri's signature vocals.The subsequent sections are drawn from their benchmark album *The Clockwork Fable*; "Parts I-VIII" sees Melissa's vocals stepping into this hidden rock opera. The original album featured guests like Blaze Bayley and spanned over three hours, complete with heavy, crushing metal breaks?though here, we get a condensed fifteen-minute version.The "Parts IX-XIII" sequence features Arjen as a guest?acting more as narrator than singer, evoking the Ayreon sound?alongside Melissa's enchanting, sultry, angelic vocals. The mood shifts from medieval-folk gentleness to doom metal reminiscent of Black Sabbath. The finale is sweeter and remains wonderfully eclectic, continuing to transport the listener into a symphonic, Tolkien-esque world.The conclusion comes with the brief "Parts XIV-XV," featuring Luke on vocals and a solemn, excellent melody with Middle Eastern and Japanese influences.Gandalf's Fist celebrates its sprawling 2016 album by weaving together its sixteen musical chapters; it serves as a "fake" compilation that highlights this complete, uninterrupted, masterful, and admirable work. Excellent. (4.5)
items._genre: neo-prog / progressive rock / symphonic rock / folk metal
items._cn_summary: Gandalf's Fist 的这张作品是对其 2016 年概念专辑的重新编排，将原本横跨三小时的摇滚歌剧浓缩为精选篇章。开篇十五分钟融合了新前卫、华丽重金属与民谣元素，配器宏大、过渡恢弘，弦乐烘托下人声成为主导。随后各部分依次展开：Melissa 的声线注入隐秘歌剧质感，Arjen 以叙事者身份客串带来与 Ayreon 相似的氛围，段落从中世纪民谣的柔和滑入黑色安息日式的厄运金属，最终收束于中东与日本音律交织的短篇。整张专辑更像是一部托尔金式奇幻世界的声乐编年史，结构庞大、风格杂糅，但本质上仍属于传统摇滚语汇下的概念化操作，与纯实验或电子路径存在距离。

items.body: Every track has a voice on it this time. Trentemøller releases trentemøller, his self-titled album, on 13 November 2026 through his own label In My Room, on red vinyl, CD, cassette and digital. The first single, Terrified, arrived on 28 August with a video directed by Jonas Bjerre of the Danish band Mew, who also sings on it. It is the first Trentemøller album on which every one of the ten songs carries vocals. trentemøller by Trentemøller Inside the new Trentemøller album The running order is “Swerve”, “Terrified”, “Visceral”, “Johnny Boy”, “Halved”, “Your Love Walks Alone”, “To Mist”, “Coyote”, “Crash” and “White Hallways”. Anders Trentemøller wrote, played, produced and mixed the record himself and released it on his own label. The guest list runs through the tracklist: Vienna-based singer Sakura on “Swerve” and “Visceral”, Anika on “Johnny Boy”, Bjerre on “Terrified”, Sune Rose Wagner of The Raveonettes on “Your Love Walks Alone” and Madeline Johnston, who records as Midwife, on “Halved”, with Tan Cologne and Emma Acs also appearing. Acs now sings in his live band. Trentemøller described how he cut the album down: “The noisy got noisier, the dreamy got dreamier, the melodic got even more melodic. I was ruthless this time. Okay, kill your darlings! If a track didn’t give me a feeling of freedom, wanderlust, sorrow, love or that pure ‘I don’t give a fuck’ feeling … It was gone.” “Terrified” runs three minutes and was rebuilt after the fact. On the change he made to it, Trentemøller said: “‘Terrified’ is probably the poppiest song on the album. In its original form it sounded a lot more shoegazey, but I wanted it to be crisper and clearer, less washed out. So I went for synths that almost sound like human voices, with a magical, otherworldly quality to them. When the instrumental was done, I sent it to Jonas Bjerre with a few melody ideas, which he took further while adding new melodies of his own.” Bjerre wrote the lyrics and explained where they came from: “I think sometimes when you dream about things that make you fearful and uneasy, it’s your mind trying to prepare you for any scenario, like you’re processing catastrophes that have not and may not ever happen.” He also shot and compiled the video, with cinematography shared with Sarah Liisborg, and Mackenzie Stith, Yuting Liu and Agnete Hegelund appearing in it. Trentemøller tour dates 2027 The full band play fourteen European shows in February and March 2027, opening in Berlin and closing at home in Copenhagen, with two nights at Ancienne Belgique in Brussels. Trentemøller said he intends to play the album in full on the run: “Now I can’t wait to play these songs live with my band. For the first time ever, I’m going to play the whole album, start to end. Every single song!” 27.02.2027 – Berlin, DE – Huxley’s Neue Welt 01.03.2027 – Munich, DE – Kesselhaus 02.03.2027 – Bern, CH – Bierhübeli 03.03.2027 – Paris, FR – La Cigale 05.03.2027 – Brussels, BE – Ancienne Belgique 06.03.2027 – Brussels, BE – Ancienne Belgique 07.03.2027 – Luxembourg, LU – Den Atelier 09.03.2027 – Amsterdam, NL – Paradiso 11.03.2027 – London, UK – Electric Ballroom 13.03.2027 – Cologne, DE – Carlswerk Victoria 17.03.2027 – Oslo, NO – Rockefeller 18.03.2027 – Gothenburg, SE – Pustervik 19.03.2027 – Stockholm, SE – Slaktkyrkan 20.03.2027 – Copenhagen, DK – VEGA About Trentemøller Anders Trentemøller was born on 16 October 1972 and works from Copenhagen. He came out of the Danish club scene in the early 2000s and released his debut album “The Last Resort” in October 2006 on Poker Flat Recordings, a record built on slow, textured electronics rather than dancefloor tempos. He founded his own label, In My Room, around 2010 and has released everything since through it. “Into the Great Wide Yonder” arrived on 28 May 2010 and pulled guitars and live drums into the arrangements. “Lost” followed in September 2013 with a long guest list, then “Fixion” in September 2016 and “Obverse” on 27 September 2019. “Memoria” came out on 11 February 2022, trailed by the singles “In the Gloaming”, “All Too Soon” and “No More Kissing in the Rain”, and Side-Line reviewed it on release. “Dreamweaver”, with vocals by Dísa Jakobs throughout, followed on 13 September 2024. Alongside his own records he has remixed widely. Side-Line has reported on his 2022 reworking of Blood’s “Type 9000” and on his 2025 remix of “And Nothing Is Forever” for The Cure‘s “Mixes of a Lost World”. Side-Line also reported in 2023 that he was among the acts announced to support Depeche Mode on their European tour. The self-titled album on 13 November is his first since “Dreamweaver”.

items.body: Four remixers, four tracks, one record. PIG, the industrial project of Raymond Watts, release Merciless on 25 September 2026 through Armalyte Industries, on vinyl and digital. All four source tracks come from the 2022 album “The Merciless Light”, and each is handed to a different name from the industrial and electronic underground. Merciless by PIG What is on the PIG ‘Merciless’ remix record The running order is “Obliteration Liberation” remixed by Clock DVA, “Speak Of Sin” in a StabWalt extended remix, “No Yes More Less” reworked by Pitchshifter, and “The Merciless Light” remixed by Günter Schulz. StabWalt is Walter Flakus of Stabbing Westward; Schulz played guitar in KMFDM and now plays in Slick Idiot, and his remix of “The Merciless Light” first appeared on the limited “Tree Of Blood” CD sold on PIG’s 2024 tour. Jules Seifert mastered the release at Epic Audio Media; the artwork is by Vlad McNeally. Three of the four source tracks appear on “The Merciless Light”, issued on 23 September 2022 through Metropolis Records; “Speak Of Sin” had already surfaced on the “Baptise Bless & Bleed” EP of 27 May 2022. The record is therefore a second pass at that album, following the 12-track remix collection “The Merciful Night” that Armalyte issued in 2025. Two vinyl editions are on sale through Bandcamp. The North American pressing runs to 200 copies on black-in-white coloured, engraved vinyl; the European pressing runs to 150 copies on black and white half-and-half coloured, engraved vinyl. Both come in a black inner sleeve inside a black UV spot gloss outer sleeve. A third variant, black splatter on clear vinyl with glitter, is sold only on the current tour. Every pre-order carries an immediate download of all four tracks. Martin Atkins of Pigface, Killing Joke and Public Image Ltd is quoted on the release page in praise of the pressing. The release date lands mid-tour. PIG are on the road across North America on the Hurt People Tour with Cyanotic in support, a run Side-Line reported on when the dates were announced. The itinerary takes in three Cold Waves shows, at Pacific Electric in Los Angeles on 11 September, The Mohawk in Austin on 18 September and Metro in Chicago on 25 September, the same day “Merciless” is out. The Denver date on 28 August is a co-bill with Nitzer Ebb. About PIG PIG is the work of Raymond Watts, born 1 September 1961 in London. Watts was a founding member of KMFDM and has recorded and toured with Foetus, Psychic TV, Einstürzende Neubauten, Schaft and Schwein, as well as touring with Nine Inch Nails. He launched PIG under his own steam with “A Poke in the Eye… with a Sharp Stick” in 1988, followed by “Praise the Lard” in 1991 and “The Swining” in 1993, the last of those initially a Japan-only release. “Sinsation” arrived in 1995 and reached the United States in 1996 through Trent Reznor’s Nothing imprint. “Wrecked” followed in Japan in 1996 and in the United States in 1997, with Schulz and Sascha Konietzko of KMFDM among its contributors. “Genuine American Monster” appeared in Japan in 1999 and in the United States in 2002. Watts then released “Pigmartyr” in 2004 under the name Watts, reissued the following year as “Pigmata”, and the project went quiet. The return came with “The Gospel” in 2016, co-written and co-produced by Z. Marr, then “Risen” in 2018 and the covers album “Candy” in June 2019. “Pain Is God” followed on 20 November 2020 and “The Merciless Light” on 23 September 2022, both through Metropolis Records. “Red Room” arrived on 17 May 2024 and the “Feast of Agony” EP on 27 September that year, alongside remastered reissues of “Sinsation” in 2024 and “Wrecked” on 7 March 2025. Remix companions have run in parallel throughout: “Swine & Punishment” in 2017, “Stripped & Whipped” in 2019, “Pain Killer” in 2021 and “The Merciful Night” in 2025. The most recent studio album, “Hurt People Hurt”, came out on 22 May 2026 through Metropolis Records with Armalyte handling the European side, and Side-Line published a full review in July. A “Dirt Box” EP is due on 4 September through Metropolis, with remixes by Cyanotic, Stabbing Westward, Combichrist and Rabbit Junk. “Merciless” arrives three weeks after that, and Watts spoke about his working method at length in a recent Side-Line interview.

items.body: London post-punk project Blow Dry released the video for “Mighty Crimes” on 26 August 2026, a month after the single went out digitally on 28 July. Blair Gauld directed the clip in the Goldfields region of Western Australia, around Kalgoorlie, the Coolgardie Caravan Park and the Broad Arrow Tavern. Frontwoman Genevieve Welsh wrote the video and stars in it as a woman on the run after killing her boss. Ryan Murphy shot it, Spike Luke Wright graded it, and the crew numbered three people working without permits. How Blow Dry wrote ‘Mighty Crimes’ Welsh wrote the track with Jorge Elbrecht, who also produced it. She describes the session as a fast one: “Mighty Crimes came about really quickly, in only a couple of hours. I was in LA with Jorge Elbrecht, who co-wrote the track – he had this awesome drum beat going that had me dancing about the room, and we came up with a narrative about a woman who’s so sick of the corporate world that she kills her boss and goes on the run. She’s a little on the unhinged side of life, and that comes out more and more as the song goes on. Maybe it was writing from a character’s POV rather than a direct life experience that made it come out so quickly.” Welsh separates the joke in the premise from what sits under it: “On the surface it’s a relatable laugh – ugh, I want to kill my boss – I mean, how many people have said that before?! But there are real emotions under the humour too: the freedom and release of throwing everything away and heading out into the unknown, tangled up with the anxiety of ‘what have I done,’ and then comes the self-talk you do to convince yourself that yes you were right to make the choices you’ve made… whether you actually were or not. Or at least, that’s the mental olympics my brain goes through.” On the setting, she says the reference points were cinematic rather than musical: “It’s such a playful track combined with the Blow Dry dark humour – as soon as we recorded it I could see the imagery – a Thelma & Louise meets Tarantino meets Priscilla, Queen of the Desert getaway film, but set in the Australian outback. An off-kilter homage to my homeland.” Welsh has said the shoot itself was improvised: “There were just three of us shooting around Kalgoorlie, WA. No permissions, a rough plan, and the rest we were winging – turning up and asking on the spot. Everyone we met was so accommodating, generous and game, lots of banter and getting involved. […]” She has also said the next track goes the other way: “Our next track is softer, slower, quieter – a new frontier for us.” About Blow Dry Blow Dry is a project led by Genevieve Welsh, a Sydney-born singer based in London. She came to music from fashion and modelling, and had not sung or worked in a studio before starting the project during Covid lockdown in Sydney. She developed it after moving to London and meeting producer Jorge Elbrecht, whose other credits include Japanese Breakfast, Sky Ferreira and Angel Olsen. Welsh describes the sound as raw and theatrical, and post-punk as the closest genre label. The project has released four digital singles. “Deadbeat Guys” came out on 4 September 2025 and “Wait ‘Til Dawn” on 27 November 2025, followed by “MR. BIG” on 7 May 2026 and “Mighty Crimes” on 28 July 2026. Welsh and Elbrecht share the writing credits, Elbrecht produces, and the recordings are issued through Welsh’s own Australian entity Catalyst Distractions. Welsh also co-runs Tainted Pleasure, a Blitz Club-inspired night at The Social in London, with stylist Matt King. The “Mighty Crimes” video is Blow Dry’s third, after clips for “Wait ‘Til Dawn” in November 2025 and “MR. BIG” in July 2026. No album or EP has been announced.
items._cn_summary: Blow Dry是一支由悉尼出身、现居伦敦的歌手Genevieve Welsh主导的后朋克项目，疫情期间在悉尼开始音乐创作。2026年7月28日发行的单曲《Mighty Crimes》由Welsh与Jorge Elbrecht合作创作并制作，歌曲仅用数小时即完成，以戏谑方式讲述一位女性因厌倦企业世界而杀害老板并逃亡的故事。Welsh将表面的黑色幽默与内心真实的情绪张力区分开来，强调歌曲探讨的是抛弃一切奔向未知的自由感与随之而来的焦虑。MV由Blair Gauld执导，在西澳大利亚卡尔古利及周边取景，参考《末路狂花》《昆汀》与《沙漠妖姬》的视觉风格，三人以无许可证方式即兴拍摄完成。文章为新闻稿性质，介绍了单曲幕后创作过程与MV制作细节，未对音乐本身进行深入评论。

items.body: Texan electro-industrial act Mentallo & The Fixer see their 1994 album “Where Angels Fear To Tread” reissued by Re:Mission Entertainment on 16 October 2026. The record has never appeared on vinyl before: this edition arrives as a 2LP gatefold pressed on yellow and red inverted splatter vinyl, limited to 250 copies worldwide. Discogs lists no prior vinyl pressing in any territory. Both formats carry a new remaster by Jeff Mortimer at JM Mastering. The edition also restores the album’s original 1994 artwork, replacing the new cover the record was given for its last reissue; the artwork restoration and vinyl layout are credited to Nathan Winter at Industriarts. The vinyl gatefold prints the full lyrics alongside commentary from Gary Dassing on the making of the record. Re:Mission estimates the LP will ship on 20 November and sells it through the band’s own Big Cartel store, where a line of shirts, hoodies, tanks and posters accompanies it. The digital edition is on pre-order at Bandcamp now and reaches streaming and download platforms on 16 October. Re:Mission states the reissue exists because “it’s been important for Re:Mission to maintain high quality restorations of the original art and proper masters”, and describes the aim as bringing the record back “for the fans who’ve kept it in rotation all these years”. Where Angels Fear To Tread by Mentallo & The Fixer What the two Mentallo & The Fixer editions hold The vinyl runs to 15 tracks and the digital edition to 20. One point needs flagging: Re:Mission describes the LP as the original thirteen tracks plus two remixes, while Discogs and Wikipedia both list the 1994 Zoth Ommog CD as a fourteen-track album whose closing piece is already “Sacrilege (Grimpen Ward)”. The digital running order is: “Gargantua” “Decomposed (Trampled)” “Sacrilege” “Virtually Hopeless” “Bring To A Boil” “Coward (Submerged)” “Ruthless” “Afterglow” “Battered States Of Euphoria” “Abominations Unleashed” “Dead Days” “Atom Smasher” “Power Struggle” “Sacrilege (Grimpen Ward)” “Decomposed (Grimpen Ward)” “Sacrilege (Angel Of Death Mix)” “Decomposed (Original Mix)” “Rapid Suffocation (Lesionary Mix)” “Grim Reality (Blister Mix)” “Battered States Of Euphoria (Medina Mix)” The “Grimpen Ward” tag on tracks 14 and 15 is a remix name the brothers used during their Zoth Ommog years, and it predates the 2001 album of that name. A “Decomposed (Grimpen Ward Mix)” was already circulating on the 1995 Ras Dva compilation “There Is No Time”. The 1994 album and the editions that came before this one “Where Angels Fear To Tread” first appeared on 16 May 1994 on the German label Zoth Ommog, then a division of Music Research. Metropolis Records licensed it from Zoth Ommog and issued it in North America on 18 July 1995 with the same running order and no extra material. The album carries “Decomposed”, “Sacrilege” and “Atom Smasher”, the three tracks that reached club sets. Its most recent outing was as part of “Zothera”, the 3CD box Alfa Matrix issued in September 2014, which paired a remastered “Where Angels Fear To Tread” with a remastered “Revelations 23” and a disc of unreleased remixes titled “Apocrypha”. That box came with new cover art, which is what the 2026 edition reverses. About Mentallo & The Fixer Mentallo & The Fixer are the Texan brothers Gary Dassing, who takes the Mentallo half of the name, and Dwayne Dassing, who takes The Fixer. The two had been buying synthesizers since the mid-1980s and first recorded together in San Antonio as Benestrophe, a trio completed by vocalist Richard Mendez, whom Gary met in his final year of high school. Benestrophe cut its first song, “Pig Butcher”, in the summer of 1988 and went quiet in 1990 when the Dassings moved to Austin, where the brothers restarted as Mentallo & The Fixer. The debut album “No Rest For The Wicked” came out in 1992 on the Portuguese label Simbiose Records. “Revelations 23” followed in February 1993, the first of their records for Zoth Ommog, with Metropolis handling the US edition in 1995. “Where Angels Fear To Tread” arrived in 1994, the same year as the remix set “Mentallo & The Fixer Meets Mainesthai”. Benestrophe was revived after 1995 for the Ras Dva label, which released “Auric Fires” in 1997, and Alfa Matrix later collected that project’s archive as “Turner’s All Night Drugstore (Rare & Unreleased 1987-1997)” in 2018, covered here at the time. Dwayne Dassing left after 1997’s “Burnt Beyond Recognition”, and Gary Dassing continued alone through “Algorythum” (1999), “Love Is The Law” (2000), “Return To Grimpen Ward” and “Vengeance Is Mine” (both 2001), “Enlightenment Through A Chemical Catalyst” (2007), “Music From The Eather” (2012) and “Arrange The Molecule” (2017). Re:Mission Entertainment, which opened an official Mentallo And The Fixer merch store in 2021, has been working through the catalogue since. It put out “No Rest For The Wicked” as a 30th-anniversary edition in October 2022, a “Vengeance Is Mine” remaster in June 2025 and a 25th-anniversary “Love Is The Law” in September 2025. The label also released “Thorns”, the 2024 debut album by Dwayne Dassing’s Reign Of Roses. The brothers reunited as a duo in early 2025, when they announced a new album and their first US tour since 2006. The tour ran from September to November 2025 and took in ColdWaves XIII in Chicago, dates on the Industrial Nation run alongside Front Line Assembly, Clock DVA, Lead Into Gold and Nitzer Ebb, and a Resurrection Tour leg with labelmates Pygmy Children. No title, tracklist or release date has been made public for that new studio album since the February 2025 announcement, and this reissue is a catalogue release rather than the record announced then.
items._cn_summary: 德州电音工业组合Mentallo & The Fixer于1994年发行的专辑《Where Angels Fear To Tread》由Re:Mission厂牌首次推出黑胶版本，以250张限量双色溅染唱片形式发行，并经Jeff Mortimer重新母带处理。专辑共收录15首黑胶曲目与20首数字版曲目，数字版额外收录多首混音版本及早期Ras Dva合辑中曾出现的'Grimpen Ward'系列混音。唱片恢复了1994年Zoth Ommog厂牌发行时的原始封面设计，内页附完整歌词与乐队成员Gary Dassing的创作手记。文章详细梳理了专辑不同版本之间的曲目差异，澄清了'Grimpen Ward'这一混音名称的历史脉络，指出Re:Mission官方描述与Discogs及维基百科记录之间存在的曲目数量出入，为关注该乐队历史版本的听众提供了实用参考。

items.body: Die Krupps, the German industrial and EBM band from Düsseldorf, released “V – Metal Machine Music” on 28 August 2015 through Oblivion and Steamhammer, with distribution by SPV. The album turns 11 this year. Metropolis Records handled the North American edition. It was the ninth Die Krupps studio album and the follow-up to “The Machinists of Joy” from 2013, and it appeared as a double CD in a six-panel digipak, as a digital download and as a limited box set. Side-Line’s own pre-order item of 5 August 2015, Die Krupps announce ‘V: Metal Machine’ 2CD album for September – pre-orders accepted now!, put the release in September. Wikipedia, Discogs and MusicBrainz all give 28 August 2015 for the German edition, and that is the date used here. The title reaches back into the band’s own catalogue. “Metal Machine Music” was a 1992 single from the album “I”, named in turn after Lou Reed’s 1975 record, which Jürgen Engler has credited as an influence on the band. Engler and Marcel Zürcher wrote the music except where noted, with lyrics split between Engler and Ralf Dörper. Engler and Chris Lietz produced the record, Alex Henke recorded additional guitar and Sascha Osterland made the artwork. Disc one runs thirteen tracks: “Die Verdammten (Prelude)”, “Kaltes Herz”, “Battle Extreme”, “Fly Martyrs Fly”, “The Truth”, “Road Rage Warrior”, “The Vampire Strikes Back”, “Alive in a Glass Cage”, “Branded”, “Kaos Reigns”, “The Red Line”, “Bonded by Blood” and “Volle Kraft Voraus”. Several of those are older pieces revisited. The prelude reworks the intro tape the band used on its 2011 and 2014 tours and takes its music from Maurice Jarre. “The Vampire Strikes Back” first surfaced on a Wing Commander soundtrack in 1998, the last song the band recorded before its 1997 break. “Alive in a Glass Cage”, “Road Rage Warrior” and “Volle Kraft Voraus” are re-recordings, the last of them the title track of the 1982 album. “The Red Line” had already appeared in a different version as the B-side to the 2014 single “Robo Sapien”. Side-Line reviewed the album on 10 October 2015 and placed it next to the band’s 1990s run of “I”, “II – The Final Option”, “III – Odyssey Of The Mind” and “Paradise Now”, with the guitars sitting further forward. The review stated: “Mastermind Jurgen Engler, currently living in Austin-Texas (USA), still can’t choose between pure electronic music and guitars and succeeds in combining both in a powerful way!” The full text is in Die Krupps – V – Metal Machine Music (DCD Album – SPV/Steamhammer/Oblivion Records). Die Krupps’ ‘V – Metal Machine Music’ singles and bonus disc “Battle Extreme” / “Fly Martyrs Fly” arrived two weeks ahead of the album, on 14 August 2015, with a lyric video for the A-side that Side-Line covered in New Die Krupps video hits the net: ‘Battle Extreme’. “Kaltes Herz” followed on 16 October 2015 with “Branded” as its B-side and a promo video directed by Faderhead. “Alive in a Glass Cage” came out on 28 July 2016, re-recorded with Caliban and issued before the band’s first Wacken Open Air appearance. The second disc carries eight tracks: a Darkhaus rework of “Kaltes Herz”, a Faderhead remix of “Alive in a Glass Cage”, “Road Rage Warrior ’82” and demo versions of “Battle Extreme”, “Kaos Reigns”, “The Vampire Strikes Back”, “Kaltes Herz” and “Alive in a Glass Cage”. Dependent Records reissued both the standard and the deluxe running order digitally in 2025. About Die Krupps Jürgen Engler, Ralf Dörper and Bernward Malaka formed Die Krupps in Düsseldorf in 1980. The name comes from the Krupp industrial dynasty, and the band has pointed to Luchino Visconti’s 1969 film “The Damned” as the starting point. The debut album “Stahlwerksynfonie” appeared in 1981 and set factory noise and metallic percussion against conventional instruments. The EP “Wahre Arbeit, wahrer Lohn” followed the same year. Dörper left in 1982 to form Propaganda. “Volle Kraft voraus!” arrived in 1982 and moved toward synthesizers while keeping the metal percussion. “Entering the Arena” in 1985 dropped most of that percussion and carried the band’s first English-language material. Engler then ran the Atom-H label, signing thrash metal and hardcore punk acts, and that catalogue fed back into the band’s next decade. In 1989 Dörper started a collaboration with Nitzer Ebb on “Machineries of Joy”, a new version of the early track “Wahre Arbeit, wahrer Lohn”, which he produced with Engler. Its chart placing led to the band restarting with Engler and Dörper at the front. Guitars entered the sound in 1992 with the album “I” and the Metallica covers EP “A Tribute to Metallica”. “II – The Final Option” followed in 1993, “III – Odyssey of the Mind” in 1995 and “Paradise Now” in 1997, after which the band stopped. Engler started DKay.com the same year and released “Decaydenz” in 2000 and “Deeper into the Heart of Dysfunction” in 2002. Die Krupps returned to the stage for their 25th anniversary across 2005 and 2006, and the two “Too Much History” compilations appeared in autumn 2007. The remix album “Volle Kraft Null Acht” came in 2009 and the EP “Als wären wir für immer” in 2010, the first new material since 1997. A joint European tour with Nitzer Ebb followed in 2011. “The Machinists of Joy” arrived in 2013 as the first full album in sixteen years, and “V – Metal Machine Music” came two years later. The band re-recorded its debut as “Stahlwerkrequiem” in 2016, reported in Die Krupps re-records 1981 debut album ‘Stahlwerksinfonie’ for vinyl (incl. CD) release, and the live set “Live im Schatten der Ringe”, taped in 2014, followed on DVD, Blu-ray and 2CD, covered in Watch trailer new Die Krupps live DVD & Blu-ray (incl. 2CD) ‘Live Im Schatten Der Ringe’ – out this Friday. Engler launched the EBM side project Die Robo Sapiens in February 2018, announced in Die Krupps frontman Jürgen Engler launches EBM-only project Die Robo Sapiens, and its debut album “Robo Sapien Race” arrived in October 2022. The same spring the band announced a single and a tour with Front Line Assembly. “Vision 2020 Vision” was announced for November 2019 in Die Krupps return with a new album in November: ‘Vision 2020 Vision’, and Engler formed the industrial metal group Die Klute that year with Dino Cazares of Fear Factory and Claus Larsen of Leæther Strip. The covers album Songs from the Dark Side of Heaven came in March 2021, and the band’s first live recording, from 1981, was issued as The Big Industrial Bang on CD and DVD in April of the same year. Marcel Zürcher, guitarist since 2005, left in 2023, and Nils Finkeisen covered guitar until 2024. The line-up is now Engler on vocals, guitars and keyboards, Dörper on keyboards, synthesizers and programming, Paul Keller on drums and Dylan Smith on guitars. In August 2025 the band signed a multi-album deal with Dependent Records, reported in Die Krupps sign multi-album deal with Dependent Records; new album due in 2026, and followed it with the tour-only EP Will nicht – MUSS! / On Collision Course. Engler and Dörper looked back across the run in Ralf Dörper interview on why Die Krupps still won’t behave and Die Krupps interview on the 45 Years of Industrial Steel North America Tour. Eleven years on, “V – Metal Machine Music” sits between “The Machinists of Joy” and “Vision 2020 Vision” in that sequence.
items._cn_summary: Die Krupps于2015年发行的第九张录音室专辑《V – Metal Machine Music》以双CD形式推出，将工业电子与EBM基因置于更突出的吉他框架中。专辑延续了乐队1990年代《I》《II》《III》《Paradise Now》时期的混合路线，核心创作者Jürgen Engler在纯电子与吉他编曲之间游走，将两者整合为一种厚重且机械化的声响。标题致敬Lou Reed 1975年的同名专辑，Engler本人曾表示这是乐队的重要影响来源。曲目方面包含重新演绎的旧作：序曲取材自乐队2011与2014年巡演使用的引言段落并融合Maurice Jarre的音乐素材；1997年乐队解散前录制的《The Vampire Strikes Back》此次被重新收录；数首早期作品以重录形式呈现。整体制作由Engler与Chris Lietz完成，发行渠道为Oblivion与Steamhammer厂牌，北美版由Metropolis Records发行。

items.body: Oxford has certain ghosts to answer for. The Thames Valley once produced a generation of guitar bands who treated distortion less as decoration than physical substance, something capable of swallowing melody and returning it in stranger shapes. Violet Oscillation comes from that same ground, and on their debut EP, it has become clear to me that all those who seek sounds deeply aware of the inheritance without behaving like a museum exhibit dedicated to 1991. Across five densely layered songs, guitars buckle, blur, bend sideways, then dissolve into banks of reverb where the human voice becomes another instrument caught inside the machinery. Veil establishes the method with glide guitar bent into great slabs of pitch and pressure. The My Bloody Valentine connection is obvious, yet Violet Oscillation understands that imitation begins where curiosity ends. Their guitars keep shifting underfoot, with chords smeared across one another until melody appears almost accidentally through the distortion. The track has tremendous weight, though its movement remains oddly weightless, as if the amplifier stacks had somehow learned to levitate. All Meaning Was Whole pushes further into that overloaded guitar language. Layers accumulate until individual parts become difficult to isolate, which is precisely where the song becomes interesting. There are melodies buried everywhere, rising briefly from the mass before being folded back into it. The performance has the strange emotional scale that made shoegaze compelling in the first place: private feeling blown up to architectural dimensions, bedroom uncertainty projected across a wall of amplifiers. Primordial Learning, featuring Abstract in Sound, shifts toward the airier end of Violet Oscillation’s vocabulary. Slowdive and Cocteau Twins hover somewhere in the ancestry, particularly in the suspended vocals and soft-focus guitar treatments, while the arrangement maintains a restless interior motion. Voices drift through overlapping effects, guitars hang in elongated chords, and each new layer seems to widen the room by another impossible few feet. Ethereal, featuring Abstract in Sound, maintains Slowdive’s gauzy style with a slow-moving layer of dreamy haze that resonates with an otherworldly, euphoric energy. It flutters, with stereo channels moving apart and together, creating a calming yet disorienting effect, reminiscent of floating upward and descending toward murmuring angels, or entering a parallel universe. The song smoothly shifts to a gentle marching drum beat as it fades away. Visual Snow closes the EP in a thick blur of texture, melody, and accumulated noise. The title fits: everything seems visible yet unstable, as though the music were being perceived through an electrical haze. Lovesliescrushing provides another useful reference point here, especially in the manner that guitar becomes atmosphere, mass, and motion simultaneously. Violet Oscillation have spent years embedded in shoegaze culture through Pedal Partners, signature effects pedals, and connections extending from Kevin Shields’ Fender Blender launch to Slowdive’s Simon Scott. None of that biography would mean much if these songs could not carry themselves. Fortunately, they can. it has become clear to me that all those who seek finds Violet Oscillation treating shoegaze as a living vocabulary: guitars bent beyond polite recognition, voices suspended inside great clouds of amplification, and four songs determined to discover how much feeling can be packed into distortion before the speakers finally surrender. Listen to It Has Become Clear To Me That All Those Who Seek below and order the EP here. it has become clear to me that all those who seek by violet oscillation Follow Violet Oscillation: Instagram TikTok YouTube Spotify The post Oxford Shoegaze Project Violet Oscillation Blooms in Reverb and Distortion on Debut EP “It Has Become Clear to Me That All Those Who Seek” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP来自牛津的Violet Oscillation，承袭泰晤士河谷吉他乐队传统，以失真与混响为物理实质而非装饰。五首歌曲层层堆叠，吉他音墙在扭曲、模糊与消融之间循环，人声成为音墙内部的另一件乐器。Veil以滑音吉他建立方法论，All Meaning Was Whole将旋律埋入过载吉他语言使其难以分离，Primordial Learning与Ethereal（均与Abstract in Sound合作）转向悬浮式人声与柔焦吉他处理，Visual Snow则以厚重质感收束全作。评论将其与My Bloody Valentine、Slowdive、Cocteau Twins、Lovesliescrushing等参照系并置，肯定其在继承谱系的同时避免成为单纯的博物馆复制品。整体属于自赏派传统内部的扎实推进，但未展现明显的跨界实验或声音设计突破，与用户偏好的实验、爵士、电子等核心取向存在距离。

items.body: I need to know And maybe we can talk about And maybe we can try to solve it Take me by the hand and take me away Heartbreak rarely proceeds with literary dignity. People sulk, contradict themselves, make declarations they abandon ten minutes later, and discover that wounded pride is a lousy substitute for company. The same voice that insists, “I don’t need you,” can soon confess, “I miss you.” French Police build their new double single, Super Over Drive / Silver, around that reversal, tracing the distance between defensive solitude and the admission that another person is still wanted. The release follows July’s Reptile / Japan, the double single that opened the Chicago trio’s new chapter with Interscope Records. On Reptile, Brian Flores looked toward companionship as a possible escape from thoughts he could not quiet. Super Over Drive takes that need into more combative territory, allowing loneliness to sour into anger before Silver strips away the posture and asks whether speaking plainly might still save something. French Police have spent the better part of their existence making romantic catastrophe sound unusually well-dressed, and these paired songs carry that instinct into bigger, cleaner arrangements without disguising the embarrassment in the words. There is still enough black-clad cool here to populate three basement clubs, but Flores sounds increasingly willing to let the mask slip, giving both songs their peculiar charge. Super Over Drive runs on a bass line with the stubborn forward motion of somebody walking home at 3 a.m. because calling a cab would require admitting the night went badly. The rhythm section keeps everything locked down while Manny Herrera’s guitar rises, retreats, then slices back through the arrangement from another angle. Flores stretches his phrasing farther than usual, holding notes until the romantic detachment begins to crack. His voice carries composure and panic simultaneously, a useful combination for a song about insisting you can live without anybody while secretly hoping somebody will notice you are drowning in your own apartment. Directed by Chris Eichenseer, the accompanying video frames the band through a sepia-tinted, abstract performance that feels appropriately unstable. Bodies blur into movement, faces appear and disappear through unusual compositions, and the muted brown tones give the footage the quality of some damaged transmission dug out of an abandoned television studio. It is moody, slightly trippy, and strange in exactly the right proportions, extending the song’s sense of emotional dislocation without explaining any of it away. Watch the video for Super Over Drive below: Silver turns the temperature down, balancing spacious guitar interplay, vocal reach, and carefully controlled escalation while leaving more room around Flores’ voice. Here the problem is communication itself: caring without saying so, sensing that something has broken, and wondering whether two people can still name the damage before it becomes permanent. The song carries guilt without theatrical punishment. Its final admissions of absence and need land with the blunt force of somebody finally saying what should have been said weeks earlier. Watch the video for Silver below: Founded by Mexican-American singer, songwriter, and guitarist Brian Flores in 2018, French Police—with Herrera on lead guitar and Rolando Donjuan on bass—came out of Chicago with obvious debts to Interpol while steadily developing a romantic severity closer to the international post-punk culture surrounding Molchat Doma, Lebanon Hanover, The Chameleons, and KINO. At the very moment a major-label deal promises to enlarge their world, Super Over Drive and Silver keep French Police focused on the smaller disaster: two people sitting close enough to speak, each waiting for the other to go first. items._cn_summary: 芝加哥三人乐队French Police发行双单曲《Super Over Drive / Silver》，延续前作《Reptile / Japan》所开启的Interscope Records合作新篇章。前作探讨陪伴作为逃离内心噪音的可能出口，而本次双单曲则将这种需求引入更具对抗性的领域：孤独发酵为愤怒，再剥去姿态，问质朴的言语能否挽回什么。乐评指出乐队擅长以精致的包装呈现情感崩塌，这次将这种本能带入更宏大、更干净的编曲，却未掩盖歌词中的窘迫。贝斯线固执前行如凌晨三点步行回家的人，吉他从另一角度切入，主唱Brian Flores拉长乐句使浪漫的疏离出现裂缝。配套MV由Chris Eichenseer执导，以棕褐色调抽象呈现情绪的失稳感。《Silver》则降温处理，腾出更多空间给Flores的声音，直面沟通本身的难题。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — After the schizophrenic two factions disbanded La Nouvelle Fronti�re, the S�guin twins went in the prog-folk direction, while the rest of the band went into the much rockier Le Match. Richard & Marie-Claire became the master of their destiny for four albums before parting ways , each having their own solo careers, Richard first teaming with Harmonium's Fiori for an album that could be considered as l'Heptade Bis. But that's another story, and we're now dealing with the duo's stunning eponymous debut album. And if the album's sleeve is something to go by, they chose the troubadour image, both on the front and back cover. Marie-Claire will design the project's album sleeves. I'm not sure at which point the twins became high-profile in La Belle Province, but they didn't sell out if you judge by their original hippie idealism. Btw, they had a more of less stable backing band of Gr�goire (bass) and Lagac� (drums), but Gilles Valiquette was a frequent contributor.Opening on the stunning medieval-like blood-curdling Som S�guin, they announce a new level from their LNF's contributions, while still claiming their original hippie folky roots (Caf� du Quai and En Toute Simplicit�). The A-side closes on the stunning Genocide, an 8-mins+ monster track that will drive shivers down your spine and its solemnity will drive the rest to your brains. What an awesome track, even 50 years down the line.The flipside returns to simpler form of folk-rock, even going to blues-rock Train du Nord. and the very Qu�b�cois Dans Ma Maison and the overlong Dis-Moi with a bit brutal change halfway though, going gradually rock. If they ever tried selling off a bit it's in the bilingual It's All Right My Friend, close to country rock, but nothing offensive (no "twang"). The album ends on the lovely and dreamy Tout Est Meilleur, but unfortunately, the second side lacks a stunner like the other face. On the merit of two stunning track on the A-side, the album is closer to 4* than 3.5*, hence the rounding up.
items._cn_summary: 这是塞甘双胞胎离开新边疆乐队后的首张同名专辑，走向带有嬉皮理想的民谣路线。A面以中世纪风格的开场曲宣告进化，随后回归民谣根源，结尾的《种族灭绝》是一首八分钟以上的庄严巨作，力量震撼。B面回到更简约的民谣摇滚形式，涵盖布鲁斯摇滚、乡村摇滚与魁北克本土风味，但缺乏A面那种震撼之作。整体制作保留了原创的嬉皮民粹主义理念，Marie-Claire负责专辑封面设计。专辑在保持艺术真诚的同时，展示了从激进步伐向更内省表达的过渡，是了解魁北克前卫民谣运动的重要文献。
